Mandating universal health insurance coverage for maternal and child services
questions.explanation: Every Woman Every Child (EWEC) is a global initiative focused on ensuring that women and children receive the health interventions they need for survival and well-being through coordinated global commitments from governments, international organizations, the private sector, and civil society. It operates within the framework of SDG 3 and complements the broader Safe Motherhood Initiative by mobilizing resources and political will for maternal and child health.
questions.question: The Every Woman Every Child (EWEC) initiative is identified as a key Safe Motherhood Initiative. Its primary focus is on:

options: Andropause affects only men over 70 years of age
Andropause involves complete cessation of hormone production
Andropause does not cause infertility in men
Andropause affects all men while menopause only affects some women
Andropause requires mandatory hormone replacement therapy
questions.question: Andropause differs from menopause in an important way because unlike menopause:
questions.explanation: A critical difference between andropause and menopause is that andropause does not cause infertility in men. Men can remain fertile even into their later years despite declining testosterone. In contrast, menopause completely ends a woman's ability to conceive naturally. Additionally, not all men are affected by andropause to a clinically significant degree, whereas all women experience menopause. These differences are clinically important for counselling patients about reproductive ageing.

questions.question: A man is found to derive sexual gratification from sexual contact with animals. Which specific term describes this behaviour, distinguishing it from a general interest in animals?
questions.explanation: Zoophilia, also called bestiality, refers specifically to sexual relations between a person and an animal, distinguishing it from a general emotional attachment to animals. It is classified among the paraphilias involving atypical objects of arousal. This is distinct from necrophilia, which involves arousal linked to corpses.

options: Its guaranteed progression to infertility in all cases
Its established link to cervical and other genital cancers
Its exclusive association with male infertility
Its role as the sole cause of pelvic inflammatory disease
Its complete resistance to any preventive vaccine
questions.question: A client is being counselled about human papillomavirus and asks why it is considered a particularly significant STI beyond causing warts. What is the key additional health concern associated with HPV?
questions.explanation: HPV is significant beyond causing genital warts because persistent infection with certain high-risk strains is strongly linked to cervical and other genital cancers. This link underpins the importance of HPV vaccination as a cancer prevention strategy, not merely wart prevention. Recognising this broader significance supports stronger uptake of vaccination programmes.

questions.question: Coprophilia is defined as sexual arousal associated with faeces, including from the smell or sight of faeces. What is Klismaphilia?
options: Sexual arousal and pleasure derived from the use of enemas
Sexual arousal from smelling urine or being urinated on
Sexual arousal from extraction or drinking of blood
Sexual interest associated with parts of the body only
Sexual pleasure derived from making obscene telephone calls
questions.explanation: Klismaphilia is defined as sexual arousal and pleasure derived from the use of enemas. This distinguishes it from coprophilia (arousal from faeces), urophilia (arousal from urine), and vampirism (arousal from blood). These less commonly discussed paraphilias involve physiological stimulation of excretory or bodily processes for sexual gratification. Clinical assessment should include screening for these conditions when patients present with unusual sexual arousal patterns.

Sexual abuse is defined as forced, unwanted, improper, or harmful sexual activity inflicted on another person. This broad definition includes various forms of sexual coercion and does not restrict abuse to physical violence alone. Understanding this definition is critical for nurses conducting reproductive health assessments of adolescents, as it enables them to identify and respond to a wide spectrum of abusive situations that may affect a young person's sexual and reproductive health.
options: Sexual abuse only occurs when physical violence accompanies the sexual act
Sexual abuse is forced, unwanted, improper or harmful sexual activity inflicted on another person
Sexual abuse is limited to penetrative acts and excludes non-contact offenses
Sexual abuse is defined only when the victim formally reports it to authorities
Sexual abuse refers exclusively to adult-on-child offenses in domestic settings
questions.question: In the context of adolescent reproductive health, which statement about sexual abuse is most accurate?
Ultrasound as a radiological assessment in female reproductive organ examination is primarily used to:
questions.explanation: Ultrasound in female reproductive organ assessment is used to examine the uterus and ovaries for structural abnormalities, cysts, or other conditions that may affect fertility. It is a non-invasive, radiation-free imaging modality that provides real-time visualization of pelvic organs. In family planning, ultrasound may be used to identify uterine abnormalities that might affect IUD placement, detect ovarian cysts that could influence hormonal contraceptive choices, or evaluate unexplained pelvic pain.
options: Determine hormonal levels by imaging the adrenal glands and pituitary
Detect cervical cancer through imaging of the cervix and surrounding tissues
Measure fallopian tube patency by visualizing dye flow under real-time imaging
Assess endometrial cell morphology for pre-cancerous changes
Examine the uterus and ovaries for structural abnormalities, cysts or conditions affecting fertility

questions.question: A woman is taught to monitor changes in the consistency and stretchiness of her cervical secretions to identify her fertile window. Which family planning method does this describe?
questions.explanation: The Cervical Mucus Method relies on observing changes in cervical mucus consistency, which becomes clear and stretchy near ovulation, to identify the fertile window and avoid unprotected intercourse during that time. This is a natural, hormone-free method requiring consistent daily observation. Its effectiveness depends heavily on correct and consistent tracking.

questions.question: A pathology report describes a breast tumour as well-differentiated with small tubular structures and a generally favourable prognosis. Which type of breast cancer does this describe?
questions.explanation: Tubular carcinoma is a well-differentiated breast cancer subtype characterised by small tubular structures and is generally associated with a more favourable prognosis than other invasive types. This differs from medullary carcinoma, which has a distinct soft, fleshy tumour appearance. Recognising histological subtype assists in prognostic counselling.

questions.question: Poor sperm motility as a cause of male infertility means that sperm lack the ability to:
options: Penetrate the zona pellucida of the oocyte effectively
Survive in the female reproductive tract for adequate time
Move effectively to reach and fertilise the egg
Carry adequate genetic material for normal fertilisation
questions.explanation: Poor sperm motility (asthenospermia) means sperm cannot move effectively enough to travel through the female reproductive tract to reach and fertilise the egg in the fallopian tube. Motility is one of the key parameters assessed in semen analysis, alongside sperm count and morphology. Causes of reduced motility include varicocele, infection, antisperm antibodies, and lifestyle factors. Assisted reproductive techniques such as IUI or IVF-ICSI can bypass motility problems by delivering sperm directly to the egg.

Genital herpes is caused by the herpes simplex virus, distinguishing it from bacterial STIs such as gonorrhoea, chlamydia, and syphilis, and from the protozoal infection trichomoniasis. Viral STIs like herpes are generally managed rather than cured, unlike most bacterial infections which respond to antibiotics. This distinction guides both treatment expectations and counselling.
questions.question: A 19-year-old presents worried after unprotected sex, asking which infection among common STIs is caused by a virus rather than bacteria, since her partner is symptom-free. Which of the following fits?
Safe motherhood is described as beginning before conception and requiring support from which level of society?
questions.explanation: Safe motherhood is a multi-sectoral endeavor requiring support from diverse sectors of the nation including the family, educators, employers, healthcare providers, community groups, and others. This reflects the recognition that maternal health is shaped by social, economic, educational, and community factors that extend beyond the health sector. A whole-of-society approach is necessary to address the social determinants of maternal health alongside clinical interventions.
options: Exclusively from the national government through funding and policy development
From multiple diverse sectors including family, community, employers and healthcare providers
Only from international agencies and non-governmental organizations globally
Primarily from women's groups and feminist advocacy organizations
Solely from health facilities and formally trained obstetric care providers
Modern adolescents engage in sexual intercourse at significantly younger ages
Adolescents now reach physical maturity earlier while marrying later than before
Contemporary media has normalized sexual behavior among younger age groups
Access to contraception has made adolescents more sexually active than previously
Government policies now permit sexual activity at lower ages than in previous eras
questions.question: Adolescent sexuality today differs from 50 years ago primarily because:
questions.explanation: Adolescent sexuality has changed over the past 50 years, with adolescents now reaching physical maturity earlier and marrying later. This creates a longer gap between biological readiness for reproduction and the social structures traditionally associated with sexual activity. This trend has significant implications for reproductive health education, contraception access, and STI prevention among adolescents.

options: Demographics, historical issues, and work-leisure balance
Communication skills, intimacy, and interpersonal relationships
Cultural variations, kinship structures, and societal institutions
Human growth across the lifespan and developmental changes
Decision making, goal-setting, and stress management within families
questions.question: The content area of Family Life Education covering 'Internal Dynamics of Families' includes which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Internal Dynamics of Families content area covers decision-making, goal-setting, normal family stresses (such as caring for elderly or dual careers), internal social processes in marital and parent-child relationships, stress and conflict management, and family crises including divorce and substance abuse. This area examines how family members relate to each other internally, as distinct from their relationships to external social institutions.

questions.question: During a perineal examination after delivery, the midwife notes a tear extending through skin and perineal muscles but sparing the anal sphincter. This is classified as which degree of tear?
questions.explanation: A second-degree tear involves the skin and perineal muscles but not the anal sphincter, distinguishing it from first-degree tears which involve skin only. Third and fourth-degree tears extend into the sphincter and rectal mucosa respectively. Correct classification guides appropriate repair technique.

questions.question: FLE promotes 'peace and unity in the family' primarily through which mechanism?
options: Legal frameworks that protect family rights
Education in conflict management, communication, and relationship skills
Religious teachings on marriage and family responsibilities
Government social welfare programmes for vulnerable families
questions.explanation: FLE promotes peace and unity in the family through education in conflict management, communication, stress management, and interpersonal relationship skills. By teaching family members to manage disagreements constructively, understand each other's needs, and build positive relationships, FLE reduces destructive conflict and strengthens family cohesion. This is distinct from external legal or governmental mechanisms, as FLE operates through internal capacity-building. SUBTOPIC 4: ADOLESCENT SEXUAL AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH

Lobular carcinoma develops from the breast lobules, which are the glands responsible for milk production. It is distinct from ductal carcinoma, which arises from the duct cells that transport milk from the lobules to the nipple. Lobular carcinoma in situ (LCIS) is rare and is considered a marker of increased breast cancer risk rather than a true cancer. Invasive lobular carcinoma is the second most common type of invasive breast cancer after invasive ductal carcinoma.
questions.question: Lobular carcinoma of the breast develops from which breast tissue?
options: The ductal cells lining the milk ducts
The connective tissue of the breast (very rare)
The breast lobules, which are glands that produce milk
The lymph tissue within the breast

questions.question: The Human Sexuality content area in FLE includes which of the following topics?
options: Demographic trends and historical issues of sexuality
Kinship systems and cultural variations in sexual norms
Reproductive physiology, sexual behaviours, and family planning
Occupational roles and economic aspects of sexuality
questions.explanation: The Human Sexuality content area in FLE covers reproductive physiology, biological determinants, emotional and psychological aspects of sexual involvement, sexual behaviours, sexual values and decision-making, family planning, and the physiological and psychological aspects of sexual response. It also addresses the influence of sexual involvement on interpersonal relationships. This comprehensive scope aims to support healthy sexual adjustment throughout the lifespan.

Early adolescence is characterised by heightened self-preoccupation and self-consciousness, often including a belief that others are constantly observing and judging them. This is a normal, transient developmental feature rather than a pathological trait. Recognising this helps adults respond with empathy rather than dismissiveness.
questions.question: A 13-year-old spends excessive time analysing her own appearance and believing peers are constantly scrutinising her. Which characteristic of early adolescent cognitive development does this reflect?
Most individuals with paraphilias report that their fantasies had developed by approximately what age, though they were afraid to discuss them?
questions.explanation: Research cited in the lecture notes indicates that most individuals with paraphilias had developed their fantasies by age 12 or 13 but were afraid to discuss them. This early onset has important clinical and educational implications. It suggests that the developmental period of early adolescence is a critical window for establishing healthy sexual attitudes and providing safe spaces for young people to discuss emerging sexual interests without shame or fear.

options: Reducing legal liability when discussing sensitive sexual health information with clients
Developing personal immunity to emotional reactions during intimate examinations
Eliminating all personal values and beliefs to provide objective care to patients
Acquiring the ability to perform reproductive procedures without emotional involvement
Becoming non-judgmental and more effective in working with clients on sexual topics
questions.explanation: Desensitization toward sexual understanding enables healthcare providers, including nurses, to become non-judgmental and more effective in working with clients on sexual topics. Acquiring knowledge and developing comfort with the vast range of normal sexual behavior allows nurses to initiate and participate in sexual health discussions without discomfort or bias. This directly improves the quality of holistic care delivered to clients.
questions.question: A nurse desensitizing herself toward sexual understanding aims to achieve which professional outcome?

questions.explanation: The argument that women's empowerment should begin during adolescence is based on the understanding that adolescence is a critical developmental window when identity, values, behaviours, and skills are being formed. Empowerment during this period creates foundations for lifelong autonomy, informed decision-making, and resistance to gender-based violence and coercion. The World Development Report 2007 supports this view, recognising that delaying empowerment to adulthood misses the most formative period. SUBTOPIC 5: SEXUAL DEVIATIONS AND PARAPHILIAS

Economic resources for empowerment are most available during adolescence
Legal frameworks only recognise the rights of adolescent women
Adolescence is the critical developmental window for establishing empowering patterns
Adolescent girls have more free time than adult women for empowerment activities
questions.question: The Women Empowerment issue in adolescent SRH argues that empowerment should begin during adolescence. This is primarily because:

questions.explanation: According to the WHO (2008), family planning is defined as the ability of individuals and couples to anticipate and attain their desired number of children and the spacing and timing of their births, achieved through use of contraceptive methods and the treatment of involuntary infertility. This definition emphasizes individual autonomy and choice—both the desire for children and the desire to limit or space them—as central to family planning.
options: Avoid all pregnancies through universal use of modern contraceptive methods
Anticipate and attain their desired number of children and control spacing and timing of births
Obtain government-approved reproductive health services at subsidized costs
Make medically certified decisions about family size with physician guidance
Achieve a specific number of children as recommended by national health targets

A woman undergoing fertility investigation is told that at birth, she already possessed her lifetime supply of egg cells within her ovaries. Approximately how many oocytes are present in both ovaries combined at birth?
questions.explanation: At birth, a female's ovaries contain approximately one to two million oocytes, the maximum she will ever have, which then progressively decline through atresia over her lifetime. This finite reserve underlies the concept of declining fertility with age. Understanding this baseline helps explain age-related fertility decline discussed in reproductive health counselling.

options: Timely and appropriate maternal health care addressing all key obstetric complications
Exclusive reliance on pharmaceutical interventions for complication prevention
Mandatory hospitalization of all pregnant women from the second trimester
Universal surgical delivery capability at all community health centers
Elimination of home delivery and traditional birth attendant involvement
questions.question: Prevention of maternal death through the Safe Motherhood Initiative requires which combination of service delivery strategies?
questions.explanation: Prevention of maternal death requires timely and appropriate maternal health care that addresses all key obstetric complications including hemorrhage, infections, hypertensive disorders, unsafe abortion, and obstructed labor. The SMI emphasizes a continuum of care approach—from pre-conception through postpartum—that integrates preventive, promotive, and curative services. No single strategy alone can address the full range of causes; an integrated, multi-component approach is essential.

options: Returning to pre-pregnancy weight within eight weeks through intensive exercise
Resuming full occupational duties within two weeks of uncomplicated delivery
Avoiding all physical activity for six months to prevent postpartum complications
Restricting breastfeeding to prevent transmission of maternal infections to the neonate
Resting and recovering physically and emotionally, and breastfeeding with support
questions.question: Which of the following postpartum behaviors is specifically recommended for new mothers?
questions.explanation: Postpartum care recommendations for mothers include resting and recovering physically and emotionally, breastfeeding and seeking support if needed, monitoring and managing postpartum bleeding and pain, attending postpartum check-ups, and prioritizing self-care while seeking help for postpartum depression or anxiety if needed. These recommendations reflect the importance of comprehensive postnatal recovery support that addresses both physical and mental health needs.

questions.question: Childbirth preparation by the mother includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Childbirth preparation as described includes creating a birth plan and discussing it with a provider, attending childbirth education classes, practicing breathing and relaxation techniques, packing a hospital bag and preparing for postpartum recovery, and having a support system in place. Home fetal heart rate monitoring using electronic equipment is not identified as a maternal preparation activity and is not standard practice for preparing for childbirth outside of medically supervised contexts.
options: Having a support system in place such as a partner
Creating a birth plan and discussing it with a healthcare provider
Performing fetal heart rate monitoring at home using electronic equipment

questions.explanation: Urinalysis in family planning examines urine for colour, odour, amount, deposit, and specific gravity, in addition to testing for albumin, sugar, and acetone. It is indicated in the presence of urinary tract infection or cystitis, and to evaluate treatment of UTIs. Understanding the normal and abnormal parameters in urinalysis allows nurses to identify conditions that may affect contraceptive choice or require treatment before initiating family planning methods.
options: Sperm presence, hemoglobin levels and pregnancy hormone markers
Hormonal content, fertility markers and pH levels exclusively
Bacterial count, white cell content and protein levels only
Colour, odour, amount, deposit and specific gravity
Viral load, antibiotic resistance profiles and crystal formation
questions.question: Urinalysis in family planning specifically examines urine for which characteristics?
The Bartholin's glands are embedded in the posterior region of the labia majora. A repeated infection of these glands results in:
questions.explanation: Repeated attacks of Bartholin's gland infection lead to a cystic condition called Bartholin's cyst, which can be recognised on palpation. A single infection typically causes abscess formation, while recurrent infection causes the duct to become blocked, resulting in cyst formation. Bartholin's cysts present as painless or mildly tender swellings at the posterior labial region and may require marsupialization if symptomatic.

options: Requesting necessary contraceptives and related supplies through the supply chain
Documenting the client's informed consent for contraceptive initiation
Scheduling follow-up appointments for contraceptive monitoring visits
Recording adverse events experienced by clients after contraceptive initiation
Gathering client feedback on the quality of family planning services
questions.explanation: The Supplies Requisition Form in family planning is used to request the necessary contraceptives and related supplies. Its logistics involve establishing a regular supply chain with clear communication channels between service providers and suppliers, and implementing inventory control measures to avoid stockouts or wastage. Effective supply management through proper use of requisition forms is critical for ensuring that family planning services are continuously available and that no client is turned away due to stock shortages.
questions.question: The Supplies Requisition Form in family planning is used primarily for:

questions.explanation: This right specifically guarantees access to services that enable women to go safely through pregnancy and childbirth, which is compromised when financial or geographic barriers prevent skilled attendance. Enforcing this right requires addressing structural barriers such as transport and facility access. Nurses can advocate for community-level solutions such as maternal waiting homes.
options: The right to equality in employment
The right to freedom of religious expression
The right to educational access generally
The right to appropriate care for safe childbirth
questions.question: A woman in a rural community is denied skilled birth attendance because her family cannot afford transport to a facility. Which reproductive right is most directly compromised?

questions.explanation: Fallopian tube damage or blockage, a leading cause of female infertility, most commonly results from pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) caused by sexually transmitted infections like gonorrhoea and chlamydia. These infections cause scarring and adhesions in the fallopian tubes that prevent sperm from reaching the egg or block the fertilised egg's passage to the uterus. Prevention of STIs through safe sex practices is therefore a direct strategy for preventing tubal factor infertility.
options: Urinary tract infections with Escherichia coli
Gonorrhoea or sexually transmitted diseases causing pelvic inflammatory disease
Candida albicans overgrowth in the reproductive tract
Systemic viral infections such as measles or mumps
questions.question: Fallopian tube blockage as a cause of female infertility is most commonly due to damage from which type of infection?
Benign tumours differ from malignant tumours primarily because benign tumours:
questions.explanation: Benign tumours are localised growths with well-defined borders that may grow large but do not spread into nearby tissues or other body parts. They are frequently encapsulated, easily removed, and tend not to recur. They exert pressure symptoms on surrounding tissues but do not invade or metastasise. These characteristics distinguish benign tumours from malignant tumours, which are aggressive, invasive, have irregular borders, can recur, and metastasise to distant organs.
options: Grow rapidly and invade surrounding tissue
Recur after surgical removal and resist body control
Cause haemorrhage, necrosis, and inflammation as they grow
Can break and travel to distant organs through metastasis
Are localised, well-defined, frequently encapsulated, and do not spread to other parts

questions.question: In family planning data collection, questions about the number of miscarriages, stillbirths, and abortions are important because they:
questions.explanation: Detailed data on pregnancy losses—including miscarriages, stillbirths, and abortions—is crucial for understanding potential risks and addressing both the emotional and physical aspects of the client's reproductive history. It aids in identifying any recurrent issues that may require investigation and informs the choice of contraceptive method. This information also provides an opportunity for empathetic discussion of pregnancy loss, which may be an emotionally sensitive area for many clients.
options: Help understand potential risks and address emotional and physical aspects of reproductive history
Determine legal eligibility for certain contraceptive methods under national regulations
Identify clients who require mandatory referral to mental health services
Establish the client's maximum future pregnancy attempts before sterilization is recommended
Allow calculation of the client's fertility potential and contraceptive failure risk

questions.question: Reproductive health care, as defined by UNFPA (2017), includes sexual health whose purpose is primarily:
options: Enhancement of life and personal relations
questions.explanation: UNFPA (2017) distinguishes sexual health from mere counselling and disease prevention, defining its purpose as the enhancement of life and personal relations. This broader conception recognizes that sexual health contributes to well-being beyond medical or reproductive outcomes. It aligns with the ICPD's holistic framework that values sexuality as a positive dimension of human experience.

questions.question: Age-appropriate sex education is listed as a topic in responsible sex education. Its primary justification is to:
options: Prevent premature sexual activity by delaying access to contraceptive information
Avoid exposing children to adult sexual content until they reach the legal age of consent
Comply with national curriculum regulations that mandate sex education in schools
Reduce parental involvement in sex education by standardizing school-based programs
Provide developmentally suitable information that empowers individuals at each life stage
questions.explanation: Age-appropriate sex education provides developmentally suitable information that empowers individuals at each life stage to make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health. It ensures that content is matched to the cognitive, emotional, and social development of the target audience. This approach increases comprehension and relevance while minimizing confusion or distress that could arise from exposure to information not yet developmentally appropriate.

Advanced cervical cancer symptoms include back or pelvic pain, difficulty urinating or defecating, swelling of one or both legs (from lymphatic obstruction), fatigue, weight loss, leakage of urine or faeces from the vagina (vesicovaginal or rectovaginal fistulae), and bone fractures (from skeletal metastases). These symptoms indicate disease that has extended beyond the cervix into adjacent or distant structures, representing locally advanced or metastatic disease with significantly poorer prognosis.
options: Improved menstrual regularity from hormonal effects
Decreased pelvic pain from nerve compression
Increased cervical mucus production and libido
Resolved vaginal discharge and pain improvement
Bone fractures, leg swelling, and leakage of urine or faeces from vagina
questions.question: In advanced cervical cancer, which of the following symptoms may develop due to regional spread of the tumour?
On examination, a woman's breast skin shows a dimpled, pitted appearance resembling an orange peel over an area of firm swelling. What does this specific skin finding suggest?
options: Normal ageing skin change unrelated to malignancy
A benign fibroadenoma with no skin involvement
A resolving haematoma from minor trauma
Peau d'orange, suggesting dermal lymphatic invasion by tumour
questions.explanation: Peau d'orange describes an orange-peel skin texture caused by dermal lymphatic obstruction from underlying tumour infiltration, a concerning sign of locally advanced breast cancer. It should prompt urgent further evaluation rather than being mistaken for a benign skin condition. This finding often accompanies inflammatory breast cancer presentations.

options: Late adolescence, driven by career planning
Middle adulthood, driven by family caregiving
Early adolescence, driven by a shift toward peer-focused relationships
Early adolescence, driven by declining physical growth
Late adolescence, driven by peer withdrawal
questions.question: A 12-year-old begins pulling away from close family involvement and increasingly seeks approval from same-age peers instead. Which developmental stage and driving process does this best represent?
questions.explanation: Early adolescence is marked by a developmental shift from family-centred to peer-centred relationships as young people seek identity and belonging outside the family unit. This is a normal, expected transitional process rather than a sign of dysfunction. Recognising this shift helps nurses and parents respond supportively rather than punitively.

options: It subjects sperm-producing tissue to higher core body temperature outside the scrotum
It produces excess testosterone that inhibits spermatogenesis
It obstructs the vas deferens preventing sperm transport
It causes immune destruction of testicular tissue
It leads to physical trauma from the misplaced testis
questions.question: Congenital undescended testis (cryptorchidism) is listed as a developmental cause of male infertility. It impairs fertility because:
questions.explanation: Undescended testis (cryptorchidism) impairs fertility because the testis, located in the inguinal canal or abdomen, is exposed to core body temperature, which is higher than the scrotal temperature optimal for spermatogenesis. Sperm production requires a temperature approximately 2–3°C below core body temperature, which is maintained in the normal scrotal position. Prolonged exposure to higher temperatures damages the seminiferous tubules. Early orchidopexy (surgical correction) is recommended to preserve fertility potential.

options: The nipple and areola area, spreading to the nipple skin
Deep internal breast tissue and the chest wall
The lobular tissue producing milk in the breast
The axillary lymph nodes draining the breast
questions.explanation: Paget's disease of the breast is a cancer of the nipple and areola area that spreads to the skin of the nipple or areola. It presents with eczema-like changes of the nipple, including redness, flaking, and itching, which may be mistaken for dermatitis. Paget's disease is often associated with underlying ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer. Diagnosis requires skin biopsy of the nipple area to identify the characteristic Paget cells.
questions.question: Paget's disease of the breast is defined as cancer affecting which specific anatomical location?

questions.explanation: Endometriosis is a hereditary condition in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, causing pain, irregular bleeding, and potential infertility. It is a leading cause of infertility in women. PCOS affects hormone levels and causes irregular cycles and ovarian cysts. Turner and Klinefelter syndromes are chromosomal abnormalities. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia disrupts reproductive anatomy through hormonal mechanisms.
questions.question: Which of the following biological conditions causes tissue similar to the uterine lining to grow outside the uterus?

options: Educating on female fertility awareness methods
Screening and managing men's reproductive health conditions
questions.explanation: Nurses specifically screen for and manage male reproductive health conditions such as prostate and testicular abnormalities as part of comprehensive reproductive health nursing. This role parallels female-focused screening such as cervical cancer checks. Including men's health screening ensures equitable reproductive health coverage across sexes.
questions.question: A nurse screens male clients for prostate abnormalities and testicular changes during routine reproductive health visits. Which broader nursing role does this activity fall under?

options: Radiation permanently strengthens breast tissue against cancer
Radiation-induced DNA damage in breast tissue increasing malignant transformation risk
Radiation exposure has no lasting effect on breast tissue
Radiation only affects bone marrow, not breast tissue
Radiation reduces oestrogen levels, eliminating cancer risk
questions.question: A woman who received chest radiation therapy for lymphoma as a teenager is now counselled about her long-term breast cancer risk. What is the underlying mechanism linking her prior radiation exposure to this risk?
questions.explanation: Radiation exposure to the chest, particularly during breast tissue development, causes DNA damage that can increase the long-term risk of malignant transformation in breast cells. This risk is why radiation history is an important part of breast cancer risk assessment. Enhanced surveillance is often recommended for women with such histories.

The nurse's role in adolescent reproductive health includes education on puberty, menstrual health, and reproductive anatomy, addressing specific needs and challenges of adolescents regarding reproductive health, and prevention of early and unintended pregnancies. This educational role equips adolescents with knowledge and skills to make informed decisions. Nursing care for adolescents must be developmentally appropriate, confidential, and non-coercive.
options: Restricting contraceptive access for adolescents to discourage early sexual initiation
Prescribing oral contraceptives for all sexually active adolescent females
Conducting mandatory pelvic examinations on all adolescent girls annually
Reporting all adolescent sexual activities to parents as part of safeguarding policy
Educating on puberty, menstrual health, reproductive anatomy, and STI prevention
questions.question: For adolescent reproductive health promotion, which of the following nursing roles is most appropriate?

options: Think through their own situations and match family planning methods to their needs
Memorize the medical criteria for each available contraceptive method
Accept the family planning method most commonly used in their community
Identify only the methods endorsed by their religious or cultural community
Document their reproductive health history for national population registers
questions.question: The concept that family planning helps 'understand own needs' through counselling means clients are helped to:
questions.explanation: The counselling principle of helping clients 'understand their own needs' means facilitating a reflective process through which clients think about their own situations—including their health, relationships, life goals, and reproductive intentions—and then match appropriate family planning methods to those needs. This person-centered approach improves method satisfaction, adherence, and long-term continuation, as clients feel ownership of their choice.

During BSE palpation while lying down, the opposite hand is used to examine each breast, so the right hand palpates the left breast and vice versa. This technique allows better reach and control across the entire breast tissue. Correct technique improves the thoroughness and reliability of self-examination.
questions.question: A woman performing breast self-examination lies down to palpate her left breast for lumps. Which hand does she use to correctly perform this palpation?
options: Neither hand; only visual inspection is used
Her non-dominant hand regardless of side

questions.question: A nurse discusses with a patient why untreated congenital reproductive malformations may go undetected until adulthood. What is the primary cause of these malformations?
questions.explanation: Congenital malformations of the reproductive system arise from abnormal development of reproductive structures during fetal life, distinguishing them from acquired conditions that develop later due to infection or lifestyle factors. Some congenital anomalies are only discovered incidentally in adulthood during fertility investigation. Early prenatal and paediatric screening can aid earlier identification in some cases.
options: Abnormal fetal development of reproductive structures

questions.question: The public health rationale for adolescent reproductive health emphasises that nearly two-thirds of premature deaths and one-third of the total adult disease burden are associated with conditions that:
questions.explanation: The public health rationale for investing in adolescent reproductive health is that nearly two-thirds of premature deaths and one-third of the total adult disease burden are associated with conditions or behaviours that began in youth. This means that many adult health problems, including cardiovascular disease, mental illness, and HIV, have their roots in adolescent behaviours and health conditions. Early intervention during adolescence can significantly reduce the lifelong burden of these conditions.
options: Developed in early childhood between ages 0–5
Resulted from poverty and poor nutrition in adulthood
Were inherited genetically from biological parents
Began in youth during the adolescent years
Emerged from occupational hazards in early working life

questions.question: Sexuality is best described as the sense of being female or male, encompassing which of the following dimensions?
questions.explanation: Sexuality has biological, psychological, social and ethical components that together shape an individual's sense of being male or female. These dimensions are interconnected and influence one another. The biological aspect relates to sexual activity, while the psychological and social components address identity, relationships, and cultural influences.
options: Physical, academic, occupational and relational components
Spiritual, emotional, cultural and cognitive components
Anatomical, cognitive, familial and economic components
Biological, social, psychological and ethical components
Hereditary, hormonal, behavioral and professional components
Only male patients, since coercion only affects men
Only hospital administrators, through improved statistics
Only adolescent patients, since adults face no coercion risk
All patients, through improved safety and reduced risk of coercion
Only staff members, through reduced legal liability alone
questions.explanation: Prevention of sexual coercion protects all patients by reducing the risk of non-consensual sexual activity within care and community settings, supporting bodily autonomy and safety. This measure benefits the broader patient population, not a single demographic group. Robust institutional protocols are essential to enforcing this protection in practice.
questions.question: A hospital implements mandatory staff training and clear reporting protocols to reduce instances of patients being pressured into unwanted sexual activity within care settings. Who primarily benefits from this reproductive health measure?

A school partnership programme reports that girls who avoid early, unintended pregnancy are more likely to remain in school and complete their education. Through which mechanism does family planning primarily improve educational outcomes?
questions.explanation: Family planning improves educational opportunities primarily by preventing early or unintended pregnancies that commonly interrupt or end girls' schooling. This mechanism links reproductive health directly to broader human capital development. Supporting continued education, in turn, further strengthens girls' future reproductive and economic autonomy.
options: Replacing the need for formal schooling entirely
Guaranteeing university admission for all girls
Preventing early or unintended pregnancy that interrupts schooling

questions.explanation: Cultural and religious beliefs continue to challenge family planning today by influencing attitudes towards its acceptability. Efforts to address this challenge include engaging religious and community leaders to promote dialogue and understanding, emphasizing the compatibility of family planning with cultural and religious values where possible. This engagement approach is more effective than confrontational strategies and helps create community environments where family planning is discussed and accessed without stigma.
options: Prevent international agencies from operating family planning programs domestically
Legally prohibit family planning services in most countries with strong religious identities
Mandate that all healthcare providers refuse to offer contraceptive counselling
Require government funding to be diverted from family planning to religious programs
Influence attitudes towards family planning requiring engagement with religious and community leaders
questions.question: Cultural and religious beliefs challenge family planning today primarily because they:
Varicocele is recognised as a medical condition that can impair male fertility. It is described as:
options: Blockage of the vas deferens from infection
Excessive heat exposure affecting sperm production
Undescended testis due to developmental failure
Hormonal imbalance caused by thyroid dysfunction
A cause of male infertility categorised under medical conditions
questions.explanation: Varicocele, an abnormal enlargement of the veins within the scrotum (similar to varicose veins), is categorised as a medical condition that can impair male fertility. It affects sperm production by increasing testicular temperature and altering blood flow. Varicocele is one of the most common correctable causes of male infertility and is found in approximately 15% of the male population and up to 40% of infertile men. Surgical or radiological correction can improve semen parameters.

HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) is a viral STI that attacks the immune system. Among the listed STIs, gonorrhea, chlamydia, syphilis, and chancroid are all caused by bacteria. HIV, along with genital herpes, hepatitis B, and HPV, belongs to the category of viral STIs. Understanding the causative pathogen is critical for determining appropriate treatment, since bacterial STIs respond to antibiotics while viral STIs require antiviral management.
questions.question: Which of the following STIs is specifically caused by a virus?
Adolescence is a transitional phase occurring between which two life stages?
questions.explanation: Adolescence is defined as the transitional phase of growth and development between childhood and adulthood. This transition encompasses physical maturation (puberty), cognitive development (abstract reasoning), social changes (independence), and emotional development (identity formation). The WHO ages this transition between 10 and 19 years. Understanding adolescence as a distinct phase between childhood and adulthood guides healthcare providers to offer developmentally appropriate services.

questions.question: The WHO definition of reproductive health states it is a state of 'complete physical, mental, and social well-being.' The word 'complete' in this definition is clinically significant because it:
options: Implies that partial well-being is acceptable in resource-limited settings
Indicates that physical health takes priority over mental and social well-being
Sets an absolute standard that requires all three dimensions to be fully addressed
Allows flexibility in implementation based on national priorities
Suggests that reproductive health can never be fully achieved
questions.explanation: The word 'complete' in the WHO definition of reproductive health is clinically significant because it sets an absolute standard requiring that all three dimensions — physical, mental, and social — must be fully addressed, not just partially. This challenges health systems that focus solely on physical or clinical aspects of care while ignoring psychological distress or social determinants. It demands comprehensive, holistic reproductive health services that address the full spectrum of well-being, not merely the absence of disease.

The cardinal ligament (also known as the transverse cervical or Mackenrodt's ligament) provides the primary lateral support to the uterus and is most important in preventing uterine prolapse. It extends from the cervix and lateral vaginal wall to the pelvic side wall. Weakness or damage to the cardinal ligament, often following childbirth, is a major cause of pelvic organ prolapse. The uterosacral ligaments provide posterior support.
questions.question: The uterus is supported in position by several ligaments. Which ligament is most important for preventing uterine prolapse by providing lateral support?

questions.explanation: The uterine wall has three layers listed from innermost to outermost: the endometrium (inner mucous lining), the myometrium (middle thick muscular layer), and the perimetrium (outer serous covering). The endometrium undergoes cyclical changes during the menstrual cycle and is the site of implantation. The myometrium provides the contractile force during labour, and the perimetrium is the peritoneal layer covering the uterus.
questions.question: The uterus is described as a hollow muscular organ. Its three main anatomical layers from innermost to outermost are:

options: Adoptive, foster, migrant, low income, military, and blended families
questions.explanation: Special Needs in Families under the FLE curriculum includes adoptive, foster, migrant, low income, military, and blended families, as well as members with chronic illness and disabilities. These categories recognise that family structures and circumstances create unique challenges requiring tailored educational approaches. FLE programmes must be inclusive of diverse family forms to be effective across different socioeconomic and cultural contexts.
questions.question: Special Needs in Families, listed under the Internal Dynamics of Families in FLE content, specifically includes families such as:

questions.explanation: The concept that sexuality exists from birth until death has a direct nursing implication: nurses must address sexual health needs across all age groups and life stages, not just during reproductive years. This means that children, adolescents, adults, and the elderly all have legitimate sexual health needs. Holistic nursing care requires that these needs be acknowledged and addressed appropriately at every stage of life.
options: Sexuality education should only be initiated when patients raise concerns directly
Nurses should only provide sexual health education to adults of reproductive age
Sexual health interventions are most critical during adolescence and early adulthood
Elderly patients do not require sexual health assessments due to menopause or andropause
Nurses must address sexual health needs across all age groups and life stages
questions.question: The statement that sexuality 'exists throughout a person's life and is a part of us from birth until death' emphasizes which nursing implication?

options: To prevent transmission of infection between provider and client
To improve the client's comfort during the procedure
To reduce the need for informed consent
To shorten the duration of the examination
To eliminate the need for specimen labelling
questions.question: A nurse dons a mask and gloves before performing a pelvic examination on a family planning client. What is the primary purpose of this precaution?
questions.explanation: Wearing protective equipment such as masks and gloves during clinical investigations primarily serves to prevent transmission of infection between the healthcare provider and the client, protecting both parties. This is a standard infection prevention and control measure in any clinical procedure involving bodily fluids. Consistent use of such precautions is essential regardless of a client's perceived infection risk.

Pedophilia involves persistent sexual urges, fantasies, or behaviours directed at prepubescent children, generally aged 13 or younger, and requires the individual to be older with a defined age gap. The distress or impairment criterion distinguishes a clinical disorder from an isolated thought. This differentiates it from other paraphilias directed at adults.
questions.question: A man reports recurrent intense sexual urges toward prepubescent children, causing him significant distress and interfering with daily functioning. Which paraphilia is described?

A woman reports pain during sexual intercourse as part of her infertility evaluation. When this same symptom occurs in a woman later diagnosed with cervical cancer, what specific clinical term is used for it?
questions.explanation: Pain during intercourse is clinically termed dyspareunia, a symptom that can arise from benign causes affecting fertility or, in more advanced disease, from cervical cancer invading surrounding tissue. Recognising the specific terminology avoids confusion with unrelated menstrual symptoms such as menorrhagia. Persistent dyspareunia warrants thorough gynaecological evaluation.

questions.question: A national reproductive health policy explicitly excludes any focus on cancers affecting the reproductive organs. Which core aspect of reproductive and sexual health is this policy failing to address?
questions.explanation: The five core aspects of reproductive and sexual health include prevention and management of reproductive cancers alongside family planning, safe motherhood, STI/HIV control, and adolescent reproductive health. Omitting cancer care leaves a significant gap in comprehensive reproductive health provision. Screening and early treatment of reproductive cancers should be integrated into routine services.

Menopause is diagnosed once menstrual periods have ceased for a full 12 consecutive months, which this woman has met. Perimenopause refers to the transitional period before this threshold is reached. Recognising the diagnostic cutoff avoids premature or delayed labelling of a woman's menopausal status.
questions.question: A 50-year-old woman has had no menstrual periods for exactly 14 months and reports hot flushes. Using standard diagnostic criteria, how should her condition be classified?

A breastfeeding mother is counselled that exclusive breastfeeding can temporarily suppress ovulation and provide contraceptive protection under specific conditions. Which mechanism underlies this method?
options: Physical blockage of the cervix by breast tissue
Direct spermicidal effect of breast milk
Continuous secretion of progestin from the breast
Suppression of ovulation through prolactin-induced hormonal changes
questions.explanation: The Lactational Amenorrhea Method relies on prolactin released during frequent, exclusive breastfeeding to suppress ovulation, providing temporary contraceptive protection under specific criteria such as exclusive breastfeeding and amenorrhoea. This mechanism is hormonal rather than mechanical. Its effectiveness declines once breastfeeding frequency decreases or menstruation resumes.

Pregnancy testing in family planning is indicated to confirm or rule out pregnancy after history and physical examinations, and to differentiate intrauterine pregnancy from hydatidiform mole (molar pregnancy). Confirming or excluding pregnancy before initiating most contraceptive methods is a critical safety step, as many hormonal and intrauterine devices are contraindicated in pregnancy. Differentiating intrauterine pregnancy from a molar pregnancy also has important management implications.
options: Diagnose early miscarriage before initiating a new contraceptive method
Determine the gestational age for calculating contraceptive initiation timelines
Screen for ectopic pregnancy in all clients with abdominal pain
Monitor the effectiveness of emergency contraception after use
Confirm or rule out pregnancy and differentiate intrauterine pregnancy from hydatidiform mole
questions.question: Pregnancy test in family planning is specifically indicated to:
Which role of the significant other is specifically related to allowing parents to rest and recover postpartum?
questions.explanation: Significant others support reproductive health specifically by providing childcare support, allowing parents to rest and recover after childbirth. This practical form of support is critical during the postpartum period when mothers are physically recovering from childbirth and establishing breastfeeding. Adequate rest and support during this period reduce the risk of postpartum complications, improve breastfeeding success, and protect against postnatal depression.
options: Providing financial support for postpartum medical expenses
Assisting with childcare to allow parents to rest
Making clinical decisions about breastfeeding and infant feeding
Accompanying the mother to all postnatal clinic appointments
Monitoring newborn development and reporting to healthcare providers

questions.explanation: Tubal ligation is a permanent surgical method for females that involves cutting, tying, or sealing the fallopian tubes to prevent sperm from reaching the egg. It is the female counterpart to male vasectomy. Reversal is difficult and not always successful, so it is intended for those certain about completing childbearing.
questions.question: A woman undergoes a surgical procedure in which her fallopian tubes are cut, tied, or sealed to permanently prevent fertilisation. Which contraceptive method has she undergone?

questions.explanation: The Lactational Amenorrhea Method is a natural hormonal method that relies on breastfeeding-induced suppression of ovulation, distinguishing it from permanent or device-based methods. It is temporary and requires specific conditions, such as exclusive breastfeeding, to remain effective. Once these conditions are no longer met, an alternative method should be introduced.
questions.question: A woman opts to rely on the natural suppression of ovulation during frequent, exclusive breastfeeding as a temporary contraceptive method after childbirth. Under which broader category does this method fall?

questions.explanation: Necrophilia is defined as a paraphilia where the perpetrator derives sexual pleasure from having sexual intercourse with dead individuals. This is one of the most extreme paraphilias and is universally illegal as it violates the dignity of the deceased and constitutes desecration of corpses. Clinically, it is associated with severe psychopathology and is exceedingly rare. It is categorised alongside other severe paraphilias in forensic psychiatric assessments.
options: Having sexual intercourse with dead individuals
Sexual activity with animals in rural settings
Observation of others during sexual activity
Making obscene telephone calls to strangers
Using enemas for sexual arousal and pleasure
questions.question: Necrophilia is defined as a paraphilia where the perpetrator obtains sexual pleasure from:

questions.explanation: The Right to Information and Education mandates that reproductive health decisions be grounded in full, free, and informed consent. This requires individuals to have comprehensive, unbiased information about all fertility regulation methods including their benefits, risks, and effectiveness. This principle underpins ethical healthcare practice and is central to client autonomy in reproductive decision-making.
questions.question: The Right to Information and Education in reproductive health includes access to full information on the benefits, risks, and effectiveness of all methods of fertility regulation, so that decisions are made on the basis of:
Which of the following symptoms is shared by BOTH menopause and andropause?
options: Irregular menstrual periods and absence of ovulation
Cessation of sperm production and vaginal atrophy
Depression, anxiety, mood swings, and hot flushes
questions.explanation: Both menopause and andropause share common symptoms including depression, anxiety, mood swings, hot flushes, night sweats, weight gain, hair loss, low libido, brain fog, and lack of energy. These shared symptoms reflect the common physiological effects of declining sex hormones on multiple organ systems. Recognising these shared symptoms helps healthcare providers offer appropriate support to both men and women experiencing hormonal changes during midlife.

questions.question: A nurse recognises that her sense of right and wrong regarding patient autonomy shapes how she advocates for informed consent. Which category of values is guiding this advocacy?
questions.explanation: Ethical values relate to an individual's sense of right and wrong and guide moral decision-making, such as respecting patient autonomy and informed consent. This differs from social values, which relate more broadly to shared community expectations. Ethical values are foundational to principled nursing advocacy.

questions.question: Responsible and safe sex is defined as engaging in sexual activities while primarily aiming to:
questions.explanation: Responsible and safe sex refers to the practice of engaging in sexual activities while taking steps to protect oneself and one's partner from unintended pregnancy, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and other potential risks. This definition encompasses both contraceptive use and STI prevention, framing responsible sexual behavior as a comprehensive protective practice rather than merely an abstinence-based or morality-based concept.
options: Comply with government policies on sexual behavior and contraceptive use
Achieve sexual satisfaction while maintaining emotional detachment from the partner
Protect oneself and partner from unintended pregnancy, STIs and other potential risks
Restrict sexual activity to marital relationships exclusively as prescribed by religion
Ensure sexual activity occurs only during identified low-risk phases of the menstrual cycle
Only individual physical health, with no broader impact
Societal and national development, beyond the individual
Only immediate family finances, with no societal impact
Only religious institutions, with no economic impact
Only environmental conservation, with no health impact
questions.explanation: Reproductive health's importance extends beyond the individual to affect families, communities, and national development, since poor outcomes reduce productivity and increase healthcare burdens. This broader impact justifies public investment in reproductive health programming as a development priority. Framing reproductive health this way supports stronger policy advocacy.
questions.question: A national health report highlights that poor reproductive health outcomes contribute to reduced workforce productivity and slower national development. This illustrates that the importance of reproductive health extends to which broader level?

questions.explanation: Surgical removal of both ovaries abruptly ends oestrogen and progesterone production, causing immediate surgical menopause regardless of chronological age. This differs from natural menopause, which results from gradual age-related ovarian follicle depletion. Other factors such as smoking or certain medical treatments can similarly precipitate early menopause.
questions.question: A woman who underwent bilateral oophorectomy in her 30s asks why she developed menopausal symptoms decades earlier than her peers. Which factor explains her early onset?
Tubal ligation is classified as which type of contraceptive method for females?
questions.explanation: Tubal ligation is classified as a permanent method of contraception for females. It involves the surgical cutting, tying, or blocking of the fallopian tubes to prevent eggs from traveling from the ovaries to the uterus, thereby preventing fertilization. As a permanent method, tubal ligation requires thorough informed consent counselling to ensure that the client fully understands the irreversibility of the procedure before proceeding.

Young girls aged 15–24 are three times more likely to be HIV-positive compared to boys of the same age. This alarming disparity reflects multiple factors including biological susceptibility of the vaginal mucosa, coercive sexual relationships with older men, limited negotiating power for condom use, and lack of access to HIV prevention services. Addressing this gender disparity requires targeted interventions that empower young women and address structural inequalities.
questions.question: Young girls aged 15–24 are how many times more likely to be HIV-positive compared to boys of the same age?
Factors that can lead to early onset of menopause include which of the following?
questions.explanation: Early menopause can be triggered by surgical removal of the uterus or ovaries (surgical menopause), as well as lifestyle factors such as poor diet, excessive drinking, and obesity, which create deficiencies in hormone levels. Medical treatments like chemotherapy and radiation can also induce premature menopause. Early menopause carries additional health risks including increased cardiovascular disease and osteoporosis from prolonged oestrogen deficiency compared to natural menopause.
options: Regular aerobic exercise and healthy diet
Removal of uterus or ovaries and obesity or poor diet
Regular cervical screening and preventive care

questions.question: A nurse is asked what alternative historical term was previously used to describe sexually transmitted infections before current terminology became standard. Which term is this?
questions.explanation: Sexually transmitted infections were previously known as venereal diseases, a term now largely replaced due to its stigmatising historical connotations. Updated terminology reflects a more neutral, public-health-oriented framing of these conditions. Awareness of this historical terminology aids interpretation of older records and literature.

questions.question: A woman has never conceived despite three years of regular unprotected intercourse with no prior pregnancy. How is this classified?
questions.explanation: Primary infertility describes a couple who has never achieved a pregnancy despite at least 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse. This is distinguished from secondary infertility, which follows at least one prior successful pregnancy. Correct classification helps direct the diagnostic workup toward relevant causes.

questions.question: Which of the following best reflects the concept of reproductive health addressing reproductive processes "at all stages of life"?
questions.explanation: Reproductive health addressing processes at all stages of life means it encompasses adolescent sexual development, adult fertility, pregnancy, childbirth, and post-reproductive concerns like menopause and andropause. This lifespan approach rejects the limitation of reproductive health to only the childbearing years. It includes the needs of adolescents, elderly individuals, and those who have completed their reproductive lives.
options: Focusing services only on women of childbearing age
Concentrating resources on maternal mortality reduction
Providing reproductive care only during pregnancy
Including adolescent, adult, and menopausal reproductive concerns
Offering contraception services exclusively to married couples

questions.explanation: The vulva is described as the external area surrounding the vagina. The female reproductive system consists of internal organs including the ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and vagina, while the vulva constitutes the external component. The clitoris extends both inside and outside the body. Understanding this anatomy is critical for nurses conducting reproductive health assessments and client education.
questions.question: Which of the following is described as part of the external area surrounding the vagina?

options: To determine legal liability for infection
To calculate national STI prevalence statistics
To assess the woman's fertility potential
To schedule her follow-up cervical cancer screening
To identify and treat exposed partners
questions.explanation: Contact tracing aims to identify and notify sexual partners who may have been exposed so they can be tested and treated, thereby interrupting the chain of transmission. It is a core public health strategy in STI control. It also helps prevent reinfection of the index client from an untreated partner.
questions.question: A woman diagnosed with gonorrhoea is asked to provide details of recent sexual partners so they can be informed and treated. What is the primary purpose of this practice?
Internet sex addiction (cybersex) typically involves which activities?
questions.explanation: Internet sex addiction or cybersex typically involves viewing, downloading, and trading online pornography or engagement with adult online content. Persons with this addiction usually prefer it over sexual relations with a live partner. The anonymous, accessible, and affordable nature of internet pornography makes it particularly addictive. Clinical consequences include relationship dysfunction, social isolation, and escalation to more extreme content. It may co-occur with other paraphilias.
options: Online dating and relationship formation only
Sharing sexual health information on social media
Cyberbullying and harassment of sexual minorities
Viewing, downloading and trading pornography or engaging in adult content online
Gaming with sexual content and avatar customisation
Telephone scatologia, valuing the victim's shocked reaction
questions.question: A man makes repeated obscene phone calls to strangers, masturbating during the call and preferring the victim's shocked reaction. Which paraphilia is this, and what does he most value during the act?
questions.explanation: Telephone scatologia involves obscene phone calls with masturbation, where the caller often derives gratification from the victim's shocked or fearful reaction. This differs from voyeurism, which requires visual observation without the victim's knowledge. Recognising the behaviour pattern helps distinguish it from other non-contact paraphilias.

The progression from HPV infection to invasive cervical cancer typically takes 5 to 15 years. This prolonged natural history is clinically significant because it provides a window for early detection through cervical screening (Pap smear, colposcopy) and treatment of precancerous lesions before they become invasive cancer. The stages include HPV transmission, acute HPV infection, viral persistence with precancerous lesion development, and finally invasion through the basement membrane of the epithelium.
questions.question: The progression from HPV infection to cervical cancer may take how many years?

options: Long-term use of combined oestrogen-progestogen therapy
Short-term use of vaginal oestrogen cream only
Any single dose of emergency contraception
Use of progestogen-only injectable contraception in adolescence
questions.explanation: Long-term use of combined oestrogen-progestogen hormone replacement therapy is specifically associated with increased breast cancer risk, more so than oestrogen-only regimens in certain populations. This informs individualised risk-benefit counselling for menopausal symptom management. Short-term or localised low-dose therapies carry comparatively lower risk.
questions.question: A woman using combined hormone replacement therapy for menopausal symptoms asks about her breast cancer risk. Which specific pattern of HRT use is most associated with increased risk?

questions.explanation: Stigma and misinformation surrounding family planning remain contemporary challenges that hinder its acceptance and access. Despite advances in contraceptive technology and availability, cultural stigma, misconceptions about side effects, and misinformation spread through social media continue to deter individuals from using family planning services. Efforts to combat this challenge include awareness campaigns, health literacy programs, and community engagement with trusted local leaders.
options: Medical advances making it unnecessary to use contraception for health reasons
Excess supply of contraceptives leading to inappropriate use without guidance
Over-reliance on family planning services displacing other healthcare needs
Universal contraceptive coverage creating complacency about STI prevention
Stigma and misinformation surrounding family planning hindering its acceptance
questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a new challenge to family planning today?
A nurse explains to colleagues that FLE draws on knowledge from psychology, sociology, biology, and education simultaneously. Why is this multidisciplinary nature operationally significant?
questions.explanation: Because FLE draws on multiple disciplines, it can comprehensively address the biological, psychological, and sociocultural dimensions of family life rather than a narrow single perspective. This breadth allows varied professionals, including nurses and teachers, to contribute to delivery. The multidisciplinary nature strengthens rather than restricts programme reach.
options: It restricts FLE delivery to medical doctors only
It covers biological, social, and psychological aspects together
It limits the scope of topics that can be taught
It requires FLE to be taught exclusively in universities
It excludes community health workers from teaching FLE

questions.question: Vaccination is listed as a preventive strategy for STIs. Which STI can currently be prevented through vaccination?
questions.explanation: Vaccination as an STI preventive strategy refers primarily to HPV vaccine (protecting against strains causing genital warts and cervical cancer) and Hepatitis B vaccine (protecting against this bloodborne and sexually transmitted virus). No effective vaccines currently exist for gonorrhoea, chlamydia, herpes, syphilis, or HIV, although research is ongoing. The HPV vaccine is particularly recommended for adolescents before sexual debut for maximum protective effect.
options: Gonorrhoea and chlamydia with combined vaccines
HIV infection with pre-exposure prophylaxis vaccines
Herpes simplex virus with antiviral vaccines

questions.explanation: The Right to Choose Whether or Not to Marry explicitly protects the right to choose to remain single without discrimination or coercion, recognising that singlehood is a legitimate life choice. It also includes protection against being required to marry without consent and the right to found and plan a family. This right challenges coercive practices including arranged marriages and social pressure to marry.
options: Select their preferred method of contraception
Choose to remain single without discrimination or coercion
Determine the appropriate age of marriage for minors
Access marriage counselling from government agencies
Register marriages under customary or civil law
questions.question: The Right to Choose Whether or Not to Marry includes the right of individuals to:

questions.explanation: Fathers play a crucial role in reproductive health during pregnancy by providing emotional and financial support to their partners and encouraging healthy behaviors such as a balanced diet, regular exercise, and attendance at prenatal appointments. Being present and supportive positively impacts the well-being of both the mother and the baby. Male involvement in reproductive health is increasingly recognized as a critical factor in improving maternal and child health outcomes.
options: Ensure that the mother follows traditional dietary practices during the pregnancy
Make clinical decisions about the type of delivery and antenatal care on behalf of the mother
Monitor the mother's compliance with antenatal clinic attendance and medication use
Restrict the mother's physical activity to protect the pregnancy from complications
Provide emotional and financial support and encourage healthy behaviors in the partner
questions.question: The role of fathers in reproductive health during pregnancy is primarily to:

options: Identify infections such as yeast or bacterial vaginosis
Detect cervical cancer through cytological analysis of vaginal cells
Assess ovarian function by measuring hormonal secretions
Visualize the endometrial lining for structural abnormalities
Confirm pregnancy by detecting human chorionic gonadotropin
questions.explanation: Vaginal cultures are laboratory investigations used to identify infections such as yeast (candidiasis) or bacterial vaginosis. These infections are common in women of reproductive age and can affect contraceptive choices—for example, yeast infections are more common with hormonal contraceptive use, and bacterial vaginosis increases the risk of STI acquisition. Identifying and treating vaginal infections before contraceptive initiation optimizes reproductive health outcomes.
questions.question: Vaginal cultures as a laboratory investigation in female reproductive organ assessment are used to:
The precaution of 'wearing protective tools like mask, gloves, etc.' during clinical investigations in family planning primarily serves to:
questions.explanation: Wearing protective tools such as masks and gloves during clinical investigations in family planning primarily protects both the healthcare provider and the client from cross-infection during procedures. Standard infection control precautions are essential when handling biological specimens, conducting pelvic examinations, or performing invasive procedures. Failure to use appropriate personal protective equipment creates risk of transmitting bloodborne pathogens and other infectious agents.
options: Reduce allergic reactions between providers and commonly used reagents
Fulfill legal and institutional documentation requirements for clinical procedures
Prevent contamination of laboratory specimens with environmental microorganisms
Comply with hospital dress code and uniform policies during clinical contact
Protect both the healthcare provider and client from cross-infection during procedures

questions.explanation: The component addressing prevention and management of complications of unsafe abortion responds to unsafe abortion being a major preventable cause of maternal mortality and morbidity globally. An estimated 25 million unsafe abortions occur annually, causing an estimated 7% of maternal deaths. Management of complications includes treatment of haemorrhage, sepsis, and organ damage from poorly performed abortions. Prevention requires comprehensive contraception access and, where legal, safe abortion services.
questions.question: The component of reproductive health addressing 'prevention and management of complications of unsafe abortion' specifically responds to which public health concern?
options: Rising rates of elective abortions in developed nations
The psychological impact of abortion on women globally
The need to restrict abortion to registered hospitals only
Legal frameworks governing abortion in Sub-Saharan Africa
Unsafe abortions as a major preventable cause of maternal mortality and morbidity

questions.explanation: The withdrawal method's effectiveness is limited primarily because pre-ejaculatory fluid can contain sperm, and precise, consistent timing of withdrawal is difficult to achieve reliably. This makes it considerably less effective than barrier or hormonal methods. Couples relying on this method should be counselled about its comparatively higher failure rate.
questions.question: A couple relies on the male partner withdrawing before ejaculation as their sole method of pregnancy prevention. What primarily limits the effectiveness of this method?
options: Sperm in pre-ejaculatory fluid and inconsistent timing
Complete absence of sperm in pre-ejaculatory fluid
Automatic destruction of sperm by vaginal pH

questions.question: Post-Abortion Care (PAC) is included as a pillar of the Safe Motherhood Initiative because:
options: All abortions are considered unsafe and require intensive medical management
Complications from unsafe abortion are a leading cause of preventable maternal death
Post-abortion care is provided exclusively as a punitive measure for illegal terminations
