Legal abortions always require intensive post-procedure monitoring and care
Post-abortion care is only needed for septic abortions in resource-limited settings
questions.explanation: Post-Abortion Care is a pillar of the Safe Motherhood Initiative because complications from unsafe abortion are a leading cause of preventable maternal death globally. PAC services treat complications such as hemorrhage, sepsis, and incomplete abortion, and also provide contraceptive counselling to prevent repeat unintended pregnancies. Addressing unsafe abortion through both PAC and access to safe abortion services is essential for reducing maternal mortality.

questions.question: Which structure of the fallopian tube is described as a funnel-shaped opening located near the ovaries?
questions.explanation: The infundibulum is described as the funnel-shaped opening near the ovaries that forms part of the fallopian tube. The fallopian tubes are passageways that carry eggs toward the uterus and have several distinct anatomical parts. The infundibulum collects the released egg from the ovary during ovulation and channels it into the tube for transport to the uterus.

This right ensures that access to reproductive health services is free from discrimination based on ethnicity, religion, or similar status. Providers withholding care based on personal bias breach professional and ethical standards. Nurses must deliver equitable care to all clients regardless of background.
questions.question: A young couple from different ethnic groups are refused reproductive health services by a provider who disapproves of interethnic unions. Which right is breached?
options: Right to equality and freedom from discrimination
Right to found a family through marriage
Right to informed choice of method

questions.question: The Cervical Mucus Method of family planning relies on which physiological change?
questions.explanation: The Cervical Mucus Method involves tracking changes in cervical mucus consistency throughout the menstrual cycle. On fertile days, cervical mucus appears clear, slippery, and stretchy (resembling raw egg white), indicating ovulation. On non-fertile days, mucus is absent, thick, or cloudy. Couples using this method avoid intercourse during days when fertile-type mucus is present in order to prevent pregnancy.
options: Changes in cervical mucus consistency throughout the menstrual cycle
Temperature variations in the body at the time of ovulation
Hormonal fluctuations measured by urine-based ovulation predictor kits
Changes in basal metabolic rate during the follicular and luteal phases
Variations in vaginal pH levels that correlate with fertile periods

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists the five pillars of the Safe Motherhood Initiative?
options: HIV prevention, family planning, newborn care, maternal nutrition and obstetric care
Prenatal care, skilled delivery, postnatal care, newborn care and family planning
Antenatal care, safe delivery, postnatal care, emergency obstetrics and cancer screening
Family planning, antenatal care, obstetric and newborn care, post-abortion care and STI/HIV/AIDS control
Contraception, antenatal care, skilled attendance, postnatal care and infertility services
questions.explanation: The five pillars of the Safe Motherhood Initiative are: Family Planning, Antenatal Care, Obstetric and Newborn Care, Post-Abortion Care, and STI/HIV/AIDS Control. These pillars represent the essential components of a comprehensive maternal health system. Together, they address the continuum of reproductive care from family planning through pregnancy, delivery, and the postpartum period, while also addressing STIs that can complicate maternal health outcomes.

questions.question: A nurse orders a specific test on a family planning client who has missed her period and reports nausea before finalising a contraceptive method choice. What is the primary indication for this test?
questions.explanation: A pregnancy test is specifically indicated in family planning to rule out an existing pregnancy before initiating certain contraceptive methods that would be inappropriate or unsafe during pregnancy. This is a standard precaution in comprehensive family planning assessment. Missing this step could result in inappropriate contraceptive counselling for an already pregnant client.
options: To screen for sickle cell trait
To rule out pregnancy before certain methods

questions.question: Menopause is diagnosed once a woman's menstrual periods have stopped altogether for:
questions.explanation: Menopause is diagnosed clinically once a woman's menstrual periods have stopped altogether for 12 consecutive months. It is a natural part of the ageing process caused by the depletion of oestrogen, FSH, testosterone, and progestogen. At the start of menopause, the ovaries stop functioning correctly, and neither ovulation nor menstruation occurs. Once menopause has occurred, a woman can no longer conceive children naturally.

questions.question: WHO defines an adolescent as any person between which age range?
questions.explanation: WHO defines adolescents as individuals aged 10 to 19 years. This range is embedded within the broader WHO category of 'young people,' which includes individuals aged 10 to 24 years. The distinction is clinically important because adolescents and young adults have different developmental needs and health risks. Early adolescence (10–14 years) differs markedly from older adolescence (15–19 years) in terms of physical, cognitive, and emotional maturity.

questions.question: The concept of 'Informed Choice' in family planning requires that clients have:
options: Their decision validated by a senior healthcare provider before implementation
Government certification confirming they have completed a family planning course
A minimum education level before being allowed to choose their contraceptive method
Accurate information to make their own reproductive choices without information overload
Written consent from their spouse before selecting any family planning method
questions.explanation: Informed choice in family planning requires that clients have clear, accurate, and specific information to make their own reproductive choices—including a choice among family planning methods—without information overload, and can help clients use each method effectively and safely. The principle of informed choice is central to rights-based family planning and ensures that clients select methods based on their own needs and values rather than provider preference or external pressure.

Exhibitionism involves genital exposure to unsuspecting individuals, with gratification typically derived from the act of exposure rather than seeking further sexual contact. This distinguishes it from frotteurism, which involves physical touching. Recognising this distinction is relevant for risk assessment and legal classification.
questions.question: A man repeatedly exposes his genitals to unsuspecting strangers in public, deriving sexual gratification primarily from the act of exposure itself rather than further contact. Which paraphilia is this?

questions.explanation: The nurse's role in menstrual health includes educating adolescent girls on the practice of good menstrual hygiene, managing menstrual disorders such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia, and providing access to menstrual products while educating on safe disposal of sanitary products. This role addresses the significant health, dignity, and well-being implications that poor menstrual health knowledge and access can have on adolescent girls.
questions.question: Menstrual health nursing involves educating adolescent girls on:
options: Good menstrual hygiene, menstrual disorders, and safe disposal of sanitary products
Hormonal replacement therapy for amenorrhea and menopausal management
Surgical management of endometriosis and uterine fibroids in adolescents
Fertility charting techniques for optimal conception planning in adults
Pharmacological management of severe dysmenorrhea requiring tertiary care

questions.question: A community health programme actively encourages couples to plan pregnancies in advance and space births appropriately, framing this as foundational maternal care. Why is planned pregnancy considered essential to safe motherhood?
questions.explanation: Planned pregnancy allows women and couples to optimise health status, such as managing chronic conditions or improving nutrition, before conception, reducing risks associated with pregnancy. This proactive approach is why safe motherhood is described as beginning before conception rather than only during pregnancy. Family planning services therefore directly support broader safe motherhood goals.
options: It guarantees a complication-free pregnancy regardless of health status
It eliminates the need for any antenatal care
It allows health optimisation before conception
It is only relevant for women over age 35
It has no measurable effect on maternal outcomes

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates the 'natural resources issue' in the rationale for adolescent SRH in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The 'natural resources issue' refers to the fact that two of the least resourced northern regions of Nigeria account for 42% of Nigeria's 15–19-year-old girls, who are demonstrably among the least educated and empowered. This regional disparity means that the girls with the greatest reproductive health needs are in the areas with the fewest resources to address them. This concentration of disadvantage demands targeted, resource-intensive interventions in these specific regions.
options: Nigeria's oil wealth being unavailable for health sector funding
Water scarcity in rural northern communities affecting hygiene
Natural environmental degradation affecting adolescent mental health
Agricultural resources being concentrated in southern Nigeria
Least resourced northern regions having most adolescent girls with low education

questions.explanation: The gynecoid pelvis, the most common type in females, is characterised by a round, shallow, and open shape that facilitates vaginal delivery. It is considered the typical female pelvis and provides the most favourable dimensions for fetal descent. Other pelvis types — android, anthropoid, and platypelloid — occur less frequently and may contribute to labour complications. The gynecoid shape differs distinctly from the more funnel-shaped male pelvis.
questions.question: The typical female bony pelvis type is called gynecoid. Its overall shape is best described as:
options: Triangular, wide at back, and deep

questions.question: A community strongly favours male children and pressures women to keep bearing children until a son is born, regardless of health risk. Which mechanism best explains how this cultural factor affects reproductive health?
questions.explanation: Cultural gender role expectations, such as strong preference for male children, can pressure women into repeated pregnancies regardless of associated health risks, worsening maternal health outcomes. This mechanism illustrates how sociocultural factors directly shape reproductive health beyond biology alone. Addressing such norms requires community-level education and engagement.
options: It has no measurable effect on reproductive health outcomes
It exclusively affects men's reproductive health
Gender roles pressure repeated childbearing despite health risk
It only affects adolescent reproductive health, not adult women
It improves reproductive health outcomes for women

questions.question: The FLE statement that 'young people age at first intercourse is decreasing' supports the rationale for FLE by emphasising the need for:
questions.explanation: The declining age at first intercourse means young people are sexually active at younger ages, making it imperative that FLE reach them early with accurate, comprehensive information before sexual debut. Delaying FLE until after first intercourse means many young people will have already taken risks without adequate knowledge or skills. Comprehensive FLE before sexual initiation is the most effective approach to promoting informed decision-making.
options: Earlier marriage to reduce premarital sex
Stricter legal penalties for teenage sexual activity
Expanded access to contraception in secondary schools
Early and comprehensive FLE before sexual debut

questions.question: In family planning data collection, which of the following is considered the PRIMARY source of subjective data?
questions.explanation: Patients are the primary source of subjective data in family planning data collection. Information gathered from patients through interviews, observations, and physical examination constitutes primary data. Secondary sources include family members, significant others, and interdisciplinary team reports. Primary data from the patient directly is the most valuable because it captures the patient's own experience, reproductive history, symptoms, and preferences, which are essential for personalized contraceptive counselling.
options: The healthcare provider's clinical observations and examination findings
The patient's family members and caregivers exclusively
Laboratory results and diagnostic imaging reports
Previous medical records from other healthcare facilities
The patient themselves through interview and self-reporting

questions.question: The Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) works as a contraceptive based on which mechanism?
questions.explanation: The Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) works based on the suppression of ovulation due to hormonal changes during breastfeeding. When a woman breastfeeds exclusively and frequently, elevated prolactin levels inhibit the hormonal signals required for ovulation. However, when breastfeeding patterns change—such as introducing supplementary feeding—its reliability diminishes significantly, requiring the use of additional contraceptive methods.
options: Prolactin-mediated suppression of the menstrual cycle causing infertility
Physical obstruction of sperm by the cervical mucus during lactation
Antibody transfer through breast milk that prevents implantation
Elevated progesterone levels during lactation that thicken cervical mucus
Hormonal changes during breastfeeding that suppress ovulation

questions.explanation: The World Bank contributes to safe motherhood primarily through providing financial resources and development funding for health system strengthening in low- and middle-income countries. As a financial institution with a development mandate, the World Bank invests in health infrastructure, health workforce development, and health system reform that collectively enable countries to deliver quality maternal health services. Financial investment is one of the most critical determinants of health system capacity to reduce maternal mortality.
questions.question: The World Bank's contribution to safe motherhood primarily involves:
options: Conducting epidemiological research on maternal mortality causative factors
Setting global clinical standards for obstetric care in developing countries
Manufacturing and supplying essential medicines for maternal health globally
Training healthcare workers in advanced obstetric surgical techniques
Providing financial resources and development funding for health system strengthening

questions.question: A survivor of sexual abuse discloses her experience to a school health provider. According to recognised guidance on adolescent reproductive health, how should this disclosure be understood and handled?
questions.explanation: Sexual abuse disclosures require a sensitive, supportive, and confidential response from health providers, combined with appropriate referral for further protection and care. Treating such disclosures dismissively or as normal exploration would fail the adolescent's safety needs. Recognising abuse accurately is essential to appropriate adolescent reproductive health practice.
options: As a normal part of adolescent sexual exploration
As an issue requiring no further provider action
As information that should be shared publicly with peers
As a matter to be addressed only by law enforcement without health support
As a serious concern requiring sensitive, supportive, and confidential response
SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
questions.explanation: The Safe Motherhood Initiative is specifically aligned with SDG 3, Good Health and Well-being, which includes explicit targets for reducing maternal mortality globally. This alignment situates SMI within the broader global development agenda rather than as an isolated programme. Tracking progress against SDG 3 targets helps measure the initiative's global impact.
questions.question: A national maternal health strategy explicitly names its overarching global target as aligned with a specific United Nations Sustainable Development Goal focused on health and wellbeing. Which SDG is the Safe Motherhood Initiative specifically aligned with?
A woman with a history of repeated Bartholin's gland infection asks how this typically presents. Which clinical finding is most characteristic of a Bartholin's cyst?
questions.explanation: A Bartholin's cyst typically presents as a unilateral, often painless swelling near the posterior introitus caused by duct obstruction; it becomes painful if infected and abscessed. This is distinct from diffuse vulvitis or vesicular STI lesions. Recognising this presentation guides appropriate incision and drainage or marsupialisation.
options: A unilateral swelling near the introitus
Multiple small vesicles on the labia minora

questions.question: Reproductive health overlaps with women's health but is not the same because:
questions.explanation: Reproductive health overlaps with but is not the same as women's health because reproductive health includes the health of both men and women. Issues such as STI prevention, infertility, contraceptive use, and sexual health communication are relevant to both sexes. While women bear a greater direct burden from pregnancy and childbirth, reproductive health as a field addresses gender-specific challenges for both males and females across the lifespan.
options: Women's health is determined by genetics, while reproductive health is socially constructed
Reproductive health is exclusively concerned with pregnancy, childbirth and postnatal care
Women's health is broader than reproductive health and includes cardiovascular concerns
Reproductive health is only relevant during the active reproductive years of adulthood
Reproductive health includes the health of both men and women across multiple dimensions
Small testicles or scrotal swelling and erectile dysfunction
Absence of periods and heavy menstrual bleeding
Cervical mucus abnormalities and ovarian cysts
questions.explanation: Signs of infertility in men include changes in libido, small testicles or scrotum swelling, erectile dysfunction, ejaculation problems, and hormonal imbalance. These symptoms may indicate underlying conditions affecting sperm production or delivery. Clinical assessment of male infertility includes semen analysis to assess sperm count, motility, and morphology, as well as hormonal testing. Early recognition of these signs is important for timely investigation and treatment.
questions.question: Signs of infertility in men specifically include changes in libido and which other symptoms?

questions.explanation: Male involvement recognises that men influence reproductive decisions and outcomes for their partners and families. Engaging men improves uptake of contraception and antenatal attendance. This component complements, but is distinct from, broader gender equity goals.
options: Male involvement in reproductive health issues
questions.question: A nurse counsels a couple that both partners should participate in decisions about family size and contraceptive choice. This reflects which reproductive health component?

options: Normal breast size, even shape, and absence of lumps
Dimpling, puckering, bulging, nipple changes, redness, or swelling
Presence of visible blood vessels and skin texture
Symmetry of both nipples and colour of areolae
Visible pulsations and movement with breathing
questions.question: In Step 1 of Breast Self Examination (inspection), a woman should stand with shoulders straight and arms on hips and look for which abnormal findings?
questions.explanation: During BSE Step 1 (inspection), abnormal findings to look for include dimpling, puckering, or bulging of the skin; a nipple that has changed position or is inverted; and redness, soreness, rash, or swelling. Normally the breasts should be usual size, shape, and colour, evenly shaped without visible distortion. Any of these abnormalities warrant prompt medical attention. Step 2 repeats inspection with arms raised to reveal different areas of the breast.

questions.question: Taking care of one's sexual health means having which of the following?
questions.explanation: Taking care of one's sexual health means having a physically and emotionally enjoyable and satisfying sexual life. For good sexual health, a person needs the knowledge, skills, and ability to make informed sexual choices and act responsibly to protect their own health and that of others. This positive, holistic framing of sexual health goes beyond disease prevention to include sexual satisfaction and emotional well-being as legitimate health goals.
options: Regular hormonal monitoring to optimize sexual health throughout life
Regular monthly STI screening regardless of sexual activity levels
Complete abstinence from sexual activity until legally married
Exclusive engagement in sexual activity with a single lifetime partner
A physically and emotionally enjoyable and satisfying sexual life

questions.question: An FLE facilitator uses an educational rather than a therapeutic approach when addressing a group's questions about relationships. What does this operational principle primarily mean in practice?
questions.explanation: An educational approach means FLE informs, teaches, and builds skills rather than functioning as clinical therapy or diagnosis. This keeps the programme accessible and non-stigmatising for participants. Referral to therapeutic services remains appropriate when a deeper clinical need is identified.
options: The facilitator refers all clients for psychotherapy
The facilitator informs and teaches, not treats
The facilitator avoids discussing personal issues entirely
The facilitator only addresses academic performance
The facilitator focuses solely on medical screening

questions.explanation: Open communication as an STI preventive strategy facilitates honest disclosure of STI status, discussion of sexual history, and negotiation of safer sex practices such as condom use between partners. This communication reduces the risk of transmission by enabling informed decision-making about sexual risk. Challenges to open communication include stigma, fear of rejection or violence, and power imbalances. Promoting communication skills is therefore an important component of comprehensive STI prevention programmes.
questions.question: The STI preventive strategy of 'open communication' between sexual partners aims to:
options: Enable partners to monitor each other's sexual behaviour
Facilitate honest disclosure of STI status and negotiation of safer sex
Encourage partners to seek testing at the same facility
Prevent intimate partner violence through dialogue

questions.question: The labia minora fuse anteriorly to form the clitoris and posteriorly to form which structure at the perineum?
questions.explanation: The labia minora fuse posteriorly to form the fourchette at the perineum. The fourchette is a clinically important structure because it is susceptible to tearing during the delivery of a first baby. Anteriorly, the upper part of the labia minora forms the prepuce over the clitoris while the lower part forms the frenulum. The fourchette separates the vaginal introitus from the perineum.

options: A stage that begins at age 10 and ends at the age of legal maturity in all countries
A stage that begins at birth and ends with the commencement of formal education
A stage exclusively defined by biological puberty changes and hormonal shifts
A stage occurring before the onset of puberty and ending by adulthood
A stage marked only by cognitive development independent of social or emotional changes
questions.question: Adolescence is characterized as a transitional stage. Which of the following best captures this transitional process?
questions.explanation: Adolescence is defined as a transitional stage of physical, emotional, and cognitive human development occurring before the onset of puberty and ending by adulthood. It encompasses multiple dimensions of development, not just biological changes. Modern trends show adolescents reaching physical maturity earlier while marrying later, changing the dynamics of this developmental period significantly.

Nipple discharge unrelated to breastfeeding, especially if spontaneous, bloody, or from a single duct, is considered a warning sign during BSE and requires prompt medical evaluation. This is distinct from normal lactational discharge in a breastfeeding woman. Early evaluation can help identify treatable underlying pathology.
options: An abnormal nipple discharge warranting prompt medical evaluation
A normal finding requiring no further action
A sign of pregnancy requiring no evaluation
A benign finding only in women over 60
questions.question: A woman notices clear fluid discharge from her nipple, unrelated to breastfeeding, during self-examination. Which finding during BSE does this represent, and what should she do?
The seminal vesicles in the male reproductive system primarily contribute to:
questions.explanation: The seminal vesicles contribute approximately 60% of the total semen volume, producing a fructose-rich alkaline secretion that nourishes sperm by providing an energy source. This secretion also contains prostaglandins and other components that facilitate sperm motility and function. The seminal vesicles are not involved in sperm production or storage; those functions belong to the testis and epididymis respectively.
options: Sperm storage and maturation before ejaculation
About 60% of semen volume with fructose-rich secretion
Neutralising the acidic environment of the vagina
Regulating FSH and LH through feedback mechanisms
Sexual intercourse becomes common and peer relationships dominate behavior
Sexual intercourse is uncommon, though fantasy and masturbation may begin
Abstract thinking fully develops and sexual orientation becomes firmly established
Puberty is complete and the adolescent forms lasting intimate partnerships
Physical maturity leads to increased interest in heterosexual relationships only
questions.question: Which of the following accurately describes early adolescence in relation to sexual behavior?
questions.explanation: During early adolescence, although adolescents may begin to experiment with their sexuality, particularly with sexual fantasy and masturbation, sexual intercourse is not common. This stage is marked by self-preoccupation, body image concerns, and separation from family towards peer focus. Concrete thinking continues from childhood, but abstract thinking begins to develop in less personal areas such as academics.

questions.question: According to the concept of sexuality, body image is best described as:
questions.explanation: Body image is defined as how we look and feel about ourselves and also how we appear to others. It is one of the key aspects of sexuality, alongside gender roles, intimate relationships, intimacy, love, and sexual arousal. These aspects are all interconnected and contribute to making a person who he or she is. Body image significantly influences sexual self-concept and behavior.
options: The physiological processes of sexual arousal and readiness
How we look and feel about ourselves and how we appear to others
The social expectations attached to our biological sex
The intimate emotional bond developed in romantic relationships
The cultural beliefs about acceptable forms of physical expression

questions.question: The pituitary gland's role in the reproductive system relates primarily to its function as a:
options: Relay center that transfers nerve signals from the hypothalamus to the gonads
Storage organ for reproductive hormones synthesized in the ovaries
Hormone-producing gland that regulates gonads through gonadotropins
Primary site of sex steroid synthesis for both male and female reproduction
Feedback receptor that monitors circulating reproductive hormone concentrations
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is a hormone-producing gland located in the brain that plays a critical role in the reproductive system by producing gonadotropins—specifically Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH)—that regulate the gonads. In females, these hormones control the menstrual cycle and ovulation; in males, they regulate testosterone production and spermatogenesis. The pituitary is part of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.

questions.question: A woman notes that after childbirth, some remnants of a thin membrane at the vaginal opening persist as small irregular tags. What are these remnants called?
questions.explanation: Following rupture of the hymen during intercourse or childbirth, the residual tissue tags are known as carunculae myrtiformes. Their presence is a normal finding in parous or sexually active women. They have no functional significance but are noted during examination.

Functional and accessible referral systems are a critical component of reproductive health because they ensure that clients with complex needs beyond the capacity of primary or community-level services can access appropriate higher-level care. Ineffective referral systems are a major contributor to preventable maternal deaths when women with obstetric emergencies cannot reach facility-based care in time. Effective referral requires reliable transport, communication, receiving facility capacity, and financial accessibility.
questions.question: Functional and accessible referral is listed as a component of reproductive health. This component is critical primarily because:
options: It reduces the workload of primary care providers
It allows health workers to discharge clients more quickly
It generates revenue for tertiary health facilities
It satisfies regulatory requirements of health ministries
It ensures clients can access higher-level care for complex reproductive health needs

questions.explanation: The NuvaRing (Vaginal Ring) is classified as a hormonal method of contraception. It is a small, flexible ring inserted vaginally that releases a combination of hormones—estrogen and progestin—over three weeks to prevent ovulation. Despite being physically inserted into the vagina, it functions through hormonal suppression of ovulation, distinguishing it from barrier methods which work through physical obstruction rather than hormonal action.
questions.question: The NuvaRing (Vaginal Ring) is classified under which category of contraceptive methods?

questions.explanation: While prenatal care encompasses routine monitoring and health promotion for normal pregnancies, the management of pregnancy-related complications and maternal morbidity specifically involves treating pathological conditions such as gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, placenta previa, and preterm labor. This distinction is important because complication management requires additional clinical skills, protocols, and often multidisciplinary involvement beyond standard antenatal care.
questions.question: The management of pregnancy-related complications is distinct from prenatal care in that it focuses on:
options: Facilitating transport for pregnant women to health facilities for delivery
Conducting routine health assessments of normal uncomplicated pregnancies
Providing health education on nutrition, exercise and antenatal vitamins
Scheduling and attending standard antenatal clinic appointments
Treating specific pathological conditions that arise during pregnancy

questions.explanation: Hereditary factors, including mutations such as BRCA1 and BRCA2, account for only a minority of all breast cancer cases, with most cases being sporadic. This means family history increases risk but is not the dominant cause overall. Genetic counselling is appropriate for women with strong family histories to assess individual risk.
options: The vast majority of all cases
Exactly half of all diagnosed cases
None, as heredity plays no role
A small minority, since most cases are sporadic
questions.question: A 42-year-old woman with a strong family history of breast cancer asks about her personal risk. What proportion of breast cancers overall are attributable to hereditary factors?
The reproductive health component of 'promoting safe motherhood, antenatal care, safe delivery, and postnatal care including breastfeeding' spans which continuum of care?
questions.explanation: The safe motherhood component spans the continuum from pregnancy (antenatal care) through delivery (safe delivery with skilled attendants) and the postpartum period (postnatal care and breastfeeding support). This continuum approach recognises that maternal and infant health outcomes depend on quality care at each stage. Antenatal care detects complications early; skilled delivery prevents intrapartum deaths; postnatal care addresses post-delivery complications and supports breastfeeding for optimal infant nutrition.
options: Pregnancy through delivery and the postpartum period
Antenatal care only for high-risk pregnancies
Postpartum care from birth until one year
Passage for the fetus during delivery
Receives the penis and ejected sperm during intercourse
Site of sperm and ovum fertilisation
Connects internal and external reproductive organs
questions.explanation: Fertilisation of the ovum by sperm occurs in the fallopian tube, specifically in the ampullary region, not in the vagina. The vagina's functions are to serve as an exit for menstrual flow, as a birth canal during delivery, and as the receptive organ during sexual intercourse. Sperm deposited in the vagina must travel through the cervix and uterus to reach the fallopian tube where fertilisation occurs.
questions.question: The vagina serves multiple functions. Which of the following is NOT a function of the vagina?

options: To satisfy an unrelated national census requirement
To gather information needed to guide safe, appropriate method selection
To generate marketing statistics for the clinic
To reduce the total number of clients served
To eliminate the need for any physical examination
questions.question: A family planning nurse compiles client histories, examination findings, and test results before recommending a method. What is the primary purpose of this data collection?
questions.explanation: Data collection in family planning is described as gathering the information needed to guide safe and appropriate contraceptive method selection for each individual client. This includes history, examination, and relevant investigations. Thorough data collection reduces the risk of contraindicated method selection.

questions.question: Pain during sex is listed as a sign of both female infertility and cervical cancer. In the context of cervical cancer, this symptom is called:
options: Deep dyspareunia from pelvic muscle spasm
Dyspareunia from cervical inflammation and tumour involvement
Apareunia from complete inability to engage in sex
questions.explanation: Pain during sex in the context of cervical cancer is called dyspareunia, resulting from cervical inflammation, tumour involvement of surrounding structures, or reduced vaginal lubrication. In cervical cancer, dyspareunia may be caused by direct tumour involvement of the vaginal walls, parametrial invasion, or radiation-related changes. In infertility contexts, dyspareunia may indicate endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease. Accurate assessment of the character and location of sexual pain guides diagnosis.

questions.question: A nurse working with a couple undergoing in vitro fertilisation provides emotional support, education on the procedure, and coordination with specialists. Which nursing role is being demonstrated?
options: Supporting couples through assisted reproductive technology
questions.explanation: Nurses support infertile couples undergoing assisted reproductive technologies by providing education, emotional support, and coordination of care with specialists, rather than performing the technical procedures themselves. This supportive role recognises the significant psychological burden of infertility treatment. Holistic support improves both treatment adherence and client wellbeing.

questions.question: A woman is told her prostate gland's female embryological counterpart contributes to reproductive function primarily through fluid secretion during arousal. Which male structure is analogous in function to the female's periurethral glands?
questions.explanation: The prostate gland contributes to reproduction primarily by secreting an alkaline fluid that forms part of semen and supports sperm viability, functionally paralleling female periurethral gland secretions. This differs from the testis, whose primary roles are hormone and sperm production. Understanding these parallels aids comprehension of reproductive anatomy across sexes.

questions.question: Which of the following symptoms of menopause specifically affect sleep?
questions.explanation: Sleep disruption is specifically identified as a menopausal symptom that affects quality of sleep in women undergoing menopause, alongside hot flushes and low energy levels. These symptoms collectively affect the emotional health of persons going through menopause. Nurses providing menopausal care must assess the impact of sleep disruption and provide appropriate interventions such as sleep hygiene education, non-pharmacological strategies, and appropriate referral for hormonal therapy where indicated.

options: The initial immune response to first sexual exposure
Allergic reaction to antibiotic treatment for the STI
Systemic spread or pelvic inflammatory disease from ascending infection
Viral replication during the latent phase of infection
Herpes recurrence triggered by stress or illness
questions.question: Fever is listed as a symptom of STIs. In the context of STI presentation, fever most commonly indicates which complication?
questions.explanation: Fever as an STI symptom most commonly indicates systemic spread of the infection or the development of pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) from ascending infection. Fever in STI contexts may indicate gonorrhoeal or chlamydial PID, syphilitic dissemination, or HIV-related immune response. Fever distinguishes complicated from uncomplicated STI and necessitates more aggressive management including hospitalisation for IV antibiotics if PID is confirmed with peritoneal signs.

The requirement for early and effective treatment of complications means health systems must provide accessible, timely, and quality obstetric care that responds promptly to emergencies. The 'three delays' model in maternal mortality recognizes that delays in seeking care, reaching care, and receiving care are key contributors to preventable maternal deaths. Addressing these delays through strengthened health systems and community awareness is essential for effective complication management.
options: Preventive medications administered routinely to all pregnant women from the first trimester
Accessible, timely and quality obstetric care that responds promptly to emergencies
Mandatory hospitalization for all pregnant women from the 36th week of gestation
Surgical delivery capability at every primary healthcare facility nationwide
Community health workers trained to perform all obstetric procedures independently
questions.question: Safe motherhood requires 'early and effective treatment of complications.' This implies that health systems must provide:

questions.explanation: The three stages of carcinogenesis are initiation (an irreversible genetic alteration from DNA mutations), promotion (a reversible stage involving changes in genome expression without structural DNA changes, mediated through promoter-receptor interactions), and progression (the final irreversible stage characterised by karyotypic instability and malignant growth). Understanding these stages is important for cancer prevention strategies targeting each phase.
questions.question: The three stages of carcinogenesis in order are:

questions.explanation: Adolescent sexuality today differs from earlier generations largely due to far greater and earlier exposure to sexual content through media, internet, and social platforms. This changes the informational and social context in which sexual development occurs, increasing the importance of comprehensive, accurate sexuality education. Providers must adapt counselling approaches to this changed landscape.
options: It has completely eliminated adolescent sexual curiosity
It exposes adolescents to content earlier and more pervasively
It delays the onset of puberty universally
It has no measurable impact on adolescent development
It only affects adolescents in high-income countries
questions.question: A clinician notes that today's adolescents are exposed to sexual content through media and technology far more pervasively than adolescents were 50 years ago. How does this primarily affect adolescent sexuality compared to previous generations?

options: Prevalence of HIV in high-density urban populations
High rates of teenage pregnancy in urban cities and peri-urban communities
Limited access to healthcare services, especially in rural areas
Shortage of specialist obstetricians in all health facilities nationwide
High cost of reproductive health technologies in all regions
questions.question: Which of the following challenges to reproductive health in Nigeria is specifically linked to geography?
questions.explanation: Limited access to healthcare services, especially in rural areas, is identified as a geographic challenge to reproductive health in Nigeria. Rural populations often lack proximity to health facilities, face transportation barriers, and have fewer skilled health workers available. This geographic inequity contributes to higher maternal and infant mortality rates in rural Nigeria compared to urban centers, making geographic access a key target for reproductive health improvement programs.

questions.question: A postmenopausal woman is refused counselling on hormone therapy because staff consider her 'past reproductive age.' Which principle is violated?
questions.explanation: Reproductive health explicitly includes management of menopause and andropause, recognising that hormonal transitions affect wellbeing beyond fertile years. Refusing care based on age contradicts the life-course approach to reproductive health. Nurses should provide counselling and support regardless of reproductive stage.
options: Reproductive health applies only during the childbearing years
Menopause falls outside reproductive health scope
Menopause management is included across the lifespan
Reproductive health is limited to fertility services

questions.question: Family planning education and awareness as a factor for growing acceptance works by:
options: Replacing cultural sex education practices with biomedical family planning training
Mandating family planning literacy as a prerequisite for healthcare access
Requiring completion of formal family planning courses before contraceptive use
Helping people understand available methods, their benefits and overcoming misinformation
Providing financial incentives for communities that achieve specific knowledge scores
questions.explanation: Education and awareness contribute to the growing acceptance of family planning by helping people understand the available methods, their benefits, appropriate use, and safety profiles, while also addressing and overcoming misinformation. Informed communities are more likely to utilize family planning services, demand quality care, and support each other in making reproductive health decisions. Health literacy is therefore a critical enabler of effective family planning program uptake.

options: It prioritizes social science research over medical or biological perspectives exclusively
It requires practitioners to hold academic degrees in at least two separate disciplines simultaneously
It mandates collaboration between religious leaders and government agencies in all programs
It restricts curriculum delivery to certified specialists in family counselling only
It draws from diverse fields including psychology, sociology and health to address family needs holistically
questions.explanation: Family Life Education being a multidisciplinary area means it draws knowledge and methods from diverse fields such as psychology, sociology, health sciences, and education to address the complex and interrelated needs of individuals and families. This breadth allows it to tackle family issues from multiple perspectives, making interventions more comprehensive and effective. No single discipline can adequately address all dimensions of family life.
questions.question: Family Life Education is described as a multidisciplinary area. Which of the following best explains why this is operationally significant?

options: Replace the need for contraceptive use when both partners are in agreement
Fulfill legal requirements for sexual activity between unmarried partners
Ensure that both partners are tested for STIs before engaging in sexual activity
Form the basis for mutual respect, trust and prevention of sexual coercion
Allow healthcare providers to verify the voluntary nature of sexual activity
questions.explanation: Consent and communication are fundamental components of responsible and safe sex because they form the basis for mutual respect, trust, and the prevention of sexual coercion. Healthy relationships prioritize communication and consent, which reduce the risk of sexual violence, STIs, and unintended pregnancies. Without consent and open communication, sexual activity cannot be considered truly safe or responsible regardless of contraceptive use.
questions.question: Consent and communication in sexual relationships are identified as key components of responsible sex primarily because they:

questions.explanation: Quality family planning counselling prioritises helping clients understand and articulate their own reproductive needs and goals before method selection, rather than rushing to a predetermined recommendation. This client-centred approach is described as the heart of effective family planning counselling. It improves the likelihood that the chosen method aligns with the client's actual circumstances and preferences.
questions.question: A rural family planning counsellor spends extra time helping a client articulate her own reproductive goals and concerns before recommending any method. Which counselling function is being prioritised?
options: Persuading the client toward a specific method
Completing paperwork as quickly as possible
Limiting the consultation to method mechanics only
Deferring entirely to the client's partner's preference
Helping the client understand her own needs

questions.explanation: Professional values are those that specifically govern conduct and expected behaviour within a given profession, such as nursing codes of ethics, distinct from an individual's personal or cultural beliefs. Understanding this distinction helps nurses separate professional obligations from personal opinions during client interactions. Professional values guide consistent, ethical practice across diverse client encounters.
questions.question: A nurse recognises that a client's professional code of ethics dictates specific expected behaviours distinct from her personal beliefs. Which category of value is being described?
High value on large families in many Nigerian cultures primarily discourages:
options: Breastfeeding and utilization of postnatal care services
Attendance at antenatal care clinics during pregnancy
Use of contraceptives and engagement with family planning services
Access to emergency obstetric care during complicated deliveries
Participation in maternal mortality reduction programs
questions.explanation: Many Nigerian cultures place a high value on large families, viewing them as a sign of wealth, social status, and continuity of lineage. This cultural norm discourages the use of contraceptives and engagement with family planning services, as having many children is often seen as desirable. Couples may feel societal pressure to have more children even if it strains economic resources and affects maternal and child health.

options: Sharing of sex toys between partners
Anal intercourse as an alternative to condoms
Oral sex to prevent STI transmission
questions.question: Which preventive strategy for STIs among adolescents involves the use of dental dams specifically during:
questions.explanation: Dental dams are specifically recommended during oral sex as a barrier to reduce STI transmission between the mouth and genitals or anus. They are listed among the preventive strategies for STIs alongside comprehensive sexual education, condom use, vaccination, abstinence, and regular testing. The use of dental dams is particularly important for preventing oral-genital transmission of herpes, HPV, and other STIs that can be transmitted through mucosal contact during oral sex.

questions.question: A woman undergoing fertility investigation is told that fertilisation normally occurs in a specific dilated segment of the fallopian tube. Which segment is this?
questions.explanation: The ampulla is the widest and longest part of the fallopian tube and is the normal site of fertilisation. The infundibulum with its fimbriae captures the ovum, while the isthmus and interstitial parts are narrower segments closer to the uterus. Fertilisation occurring outside the ampulla raises risk of ectopic pregnancy.

This component specifically addresses harmful practices such as female genital cutting that cause physical and psychological harm. It requires sustained community education and advocacy rather than a single intervention. Nurses play a key role in culturally sensitive discouragement of such practices.
options: Active discouragement of harmful traditional practices
Cancer of the reproductive tract screening
questions.question: A community continues to practise female genital cutting despite health education. Which reproductive health component specifically targets this practice?

questions.explanation: The right to privacy obligates providers to keep sexual and reproductive health consultations confidential, especially for adolescents seeking services independently. Breaching confidentiality may deter young clients from seeking care altogether. Nurses must balance parental involvement with the client's autonomy and safety.
questions.question: A 17-year-old requests contraceptive counselling and asks the nurse not to inform her parents. Which reproductive right guides the nurse's response?
Barrier methods of contraception primarily prevent pregnancy by:
options: Suppressing ovulation through hormonal alteration of the menstrual cycle
Physically obstructing the passage of sperm to prevent fertilization
Creating a chemically hostile environment in the uterus for implantation
Thickening the cervical mucus to impede sperm motility
Preventing fertilization by disrupting sperm capacitation in the fallopian tube
questions.explanation: Barrier methods of contraception—including condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps, and spermicides—work primarily by physically obstructing the passage of sperm, preventing it from reaching and fertilizing the egg. Unlike hormonal methods, barrier methods do not alter the menstrual cycle or hormonal environment. Additionally, condoms provide dual protection against both unintended pregnancy and STIs.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a role of the nurse in reproductive health as listed in the content?
options: Managing menopausal symptoms and related health concerns
Educating on puberty and reproductive anatomy for adolescents
Performing laparoscopic surgery for tubal ligation
Screening and providing treatment for male reproductive conditions
Supporting survivors of sexual and gender-based violence
questions.explanation: Performing laparoscopic surgery for tubal ligation is not identified as a nursing role in reproductive health within the content. Laparoscopic surgery is a medical/surgical procedure performed by physicians or surgeons. The nursing roles in reproductive health as identified include education, counselling, contraceptive access, STI management, maternal care, menstrual health, adolescent health, men's health, menopausal care, cancer screening, and SGBV support—all within the nursing scope of practice.

questions.question: A clinician evaluating a man with paraphilic behaviour learns that his fantasies had already developed by early adolescence, though he was too afraid to disclose them at the time. What does this history suggest about paraphilia development?
questions.explanation: Most individuals with paraphilias report their fantasies developing by adolescence, though fear of stigma often delays disclosure for years. This underscores the importance of a thorough developmental history in clinical assessment. Early identification, where possible, may allow earlier supportive intervention.
options: Paraphilic fantasies typically begin only after age 40
Paraphilic fantasies are always disclosed immediately upon onset
Fantasies commonly begin early but stay concealed
Paraphilic fantasies never persist beyond adolescence
Paraphilic fantasies are unrelated to earlier developmental history

questions.explanation: The high rate of co-occurring paraphilic behaviours indicates that clinicians should not assume a single paraphilia is the complete picture and should screen broadly during assessment. This has implications for treatment planning, which may need to address multiple behaviour patterns simultaneously. Recognising this pattern improves diagnostic thoroughness.
questions.question: A clinician notes that more than half of patients in treatment for paraphilias report engaging in three or four different paraphilic behaviours. What is the clinical significance of this finding?
options: Paraphilias are always isolated to a single behaviour
Paraphilias are unrelated to one another clinically
Only one paraphilia can be diagnosed per patient
Paraphilias frequently co-occur, so assessment should screen for multiple types
Co-occurring paraphilias indicate a different diagnosis entirely

questions.explanation: The types of norms identified in the content include descriptive norms, injunctive norms, subjective norms, social norms, and cultural norms. 'Cognitive norms' is not one of the recognized categories in this framework. Understanding the correct classification of norms helps nurses apply culturally sensitive and evidence-based care that respects the behavioral expectations operating in a patient's social environment.
questions.question: Norms are described as 'unwritten rules that shape behavior.' Which of the following is NOT identified as a type of norm?
A history of sickle cell anemia in a family planning client is important because it:
options: Automatically contraindicated all forms of hormonal contraception permanently
Can influence pregnancy outcomes and guides family planning decisions and prenatal care
Requires mandatory partner testing before any contraceptive method is initiated
Necessitates referral to a hematologist before family planning services are provided
Makes surgical sterilization the only acceptable contraceptive option available
questions.explanation: Sickle cell anemia is a hereditary condition that can influence pregnancy outcomes, making it important to document in family planning history. Awareness of sickle cell status guides family planning decisions, informs about pregnancy risks (such as pain crises, increased infections, and anemia during pregnancy), and shapes prenatal care planning. Some contraceptive methods may be preferred over others in women with sickle cell disease based on their thrombotic and hormonal implications.

questions.question: Family planning nursing is described as benefiting the individual, family and community in several ways including:
options: Eliminating all pregnancies above the national average family size
Restricting fertility to two children per family to meet national population targets
Mandating contraceptive use for all women of reproductive age in resource-limited areas
Avoiding unintended pregnancy, easing family financial pressure and improving quality of life
Reducing maternal health costs by limiting the number of antenatal consultations
questions.explanation: Contraception and family planning benefits individuals, families, and communities by avoiding unintended pregnancy, easing pressure on family finances, and generally improving the quality of life of the family. Family planning enables couples to make informed, autonomous decisions about the number and spacing of children, reducing maternal mortality, improving child health outcomes, and contributing to economic well-being. These outcomes have both individual and population-level benefits.

questions.question: About 20% of breast cancers are detected by which method rather than mammography?
questions.explanation: About 20% of breast cancers are detected by physical examination (palpation) rather than mammography, highlighting the continued clinical value of manual breast examination as a complement to imaging. This finding supports the recommendation that all women routinely perform breast self-examination as part of their overall breast cancer screening strategy. Physical examination can detect tumours that are palpable but may be missed on mammography due to breast density or tumour location.
options: Ultrasound scanning of the breast tissue

questions.explanation: Bartholin's cyst, which results from repeated infection blocking the Bartholin's gland duct, is characterised by a palpable cystic mass at the posterior region of the labia majora, where the gland is embedded. It can be recognised on palpation and may be painless if not actively infected. When acutely infected, it presents as an abscess with pain and swelling. Management ranges from warm sitz baths to marsupialization for recurrent cases.
options: Recognised on palpation at the posterior labial region
Tender mass with purulent discharge from the duct
Painful abscess visible at the anterior vaginal wall
Diffuse swelling of both labia majora and minora
Ulceration of the vestibular mucosa with erythema
questions.question: During a physical examination, the Bartholin's cyst is best characterised by which clinical finding?

questions.explanation: A history of sickle cell anaemia is important in family planning assessment because certain contraceptive methods may carry additional risks or benefits for clients with this condition, requiring individualised method selection. This is a specific example of how medical history directly shapes safe contraceptive counselling. Overlooking such history could result in an inappropriate or unsafe method choice.
options: Some methods carry added risk with sickle cell disease
Sickle cell anaemia has no relevance to contraceptive safety
It determines the client's eligibility for surgical sterilisation only
It is only relevant for antenatal, not family planning, care
It automatically disqualifies the client from all contraception
questions.question: A nurse notes that a family planning client has a personal and family history of sickle cell anaemia before recommending a contraceptive method. Why is this history particularly important to document?

questions.explanation: Postnatal care nursing supports healthy recovery for both mother and newborn through monitoring, breastfeeding support, and emotional assessment after delivery. This is distinct from prenatal care, which occurs before birth. Comprehensive postnatal support reduces risk of postpartum complications.
options: Healthy postpartum recovery for mother and newborn
Prevention of sexually transmitted infection in adolescents
questions.question: A nurse visits a new mother at home to assess wound healing, breastfeeding technique, and emotional wellbeing after delivery. Which nursing outcome is primarily supported by this activity?

questions.explanation: STIs are defined as infections that can be spread from person to person through sexual contact. Routes of sexual transmission include vaginal intercourse, anal intercourse, oral sex, and sharing of sex toys. Additionally, mother-to-child transmission can occur during pregnancy and birth. Transmission through shared toiletries, toilet seats, or casual contact is not a recognised route for most STIs, though some conditions like pubic lice may occasionally spread through close non-sexual contact.
questions.question: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are defined as infections spread from person to person through which primary route?

options: Menopausal health management and symptom control
Managing infertility and assisted reproduction exclusively
Adolescent reproductive health education and prevention
Supporting individuals experiencing sexual and gender-based violence
Maternal health and antenatal complication management
questions.question: Providing counselling and support for survivors of reproductive trauma falls under which specific nursing role?
questions.explanation: Supporting individuals experiencing sexual and gender-based violence—including providing counselling and healthcare services for survivors of abuse—is identified as a distinct nursing role within reproductive health. Nurses providing this care must be trained in trauma-informed approaches that prioritize safety, trust, choice, collaboration, and empowerment. This role requires sensitivity, confidentiality, and an awareness of the complex interplay between violence and reproductive health.

options: Pelvic inflammatory disease from untreated STIs
questions.question: A woman with a history of recurrent untreated pelvic infections is found to have bilateral tubal blockage on investigation. Which prior condition most likely caused this blockage?
questions.explanation: Untreated sexually transmitted infections can ascend to cause pelvic inflammatory disease, leading to tubal scarring and blockage, a major cause of female infertility. This is distinct from lower genital tract infections that do not typically cause tubal damage. Prevention through early STI treatment reduces this infertility risk.

The Interpersonal Relationships content area focuses on developing and maintaining relationships through communication skills including listening, empathy, self-disclosure, decision-making, problem-solving, and conflict resolution. It also covers intimacy, love, romance, and relating to others with respect, sincerity, and responsibility. These skills are foundational to healthy family relationships, peer relationships, and intimate partnerships throughout the lifespan.
options: Communication, empathy, self-disclosure, and conflict resolution
Financial literacy and economic planning for families
Civic engagement and community development skills
Academic competencies and critical thinking abilities
questions.question: The Interpersonal Relationships content area in FLE specifically develops which skill set?

questions.explanation: Vaginal cultures are laboratory investigations used to identify causative organisms responsible for abnormal vaginal discharge or infection, guiding targeted antimicrobial treatment. This differs from the Pap smear, which screens for cellular changes rather than infectious organisms. Accurate identification of infection supports both client treatment and appropriate contraceptive counselling.
questions.question: A nurse collects a vaginal swab from a family planning client reporting abnormal discharge and sends it for laboratory analysis to identify the causative organism. Which investigation is being performed?

questions.explanation: The importance of reproductive health includes protecting both the mother and the child from infectious diseases and delivering a healthy baby. It also provides complete knowledge about early pregnancy, infertility, birth control, pregnancy, and post-childbirth care. Reproductive health enhances quality of life by involving both women and men from their teens to old age through real-life approaches that support physical, emotional, and social well-being.
options: Restricting reproductive health services to specialist tertiary care facilities only
Regulating population growth according to national economic development plans
Enforcing contraceptive use among all women of childbearing age in resource-limited settings
Eliminating all forms of reproductive variation through standardized medical protocols
Protecting both mother and child from infectious diseases and ensuring a healthy baby
questions.question: The importance of reproductive health extends beyond individuals to include:

questions.explanation: The vulva refers to the external female genital structures surrounding the vaginal opening, distinct from the internal reproductive organs such as the uterus and ovaries. This distinction is fundamental to describing female reproductive anatomy accurately. Recognising the vulva as an external structure clarifies terminology used throughout reproductive health assessment.
questions.question: A woman's reproductive anatomy assessment reveals that her external genital structures lie superficial to and surrounding the vaginal opening. Which broader anatomical term describes this external area?

Only through direct contact during a caesarean section
Only through amniotic fluid aspiration in labour
questions.question: A pregnant woman with untreated syphilis asks how her infection could affect her baby. Through which route is transmission to the fetus most likely to occur?
questions.explanation: Mother-to-child transmission of infections such as syphilis can occur transplacentally during pregnancy, in addition to during delivery for some STIs. Untreated maternal syphilis can cause serious fetal complications including stillbirth. Timely antenatal screening and treatment reduce this transmission risk substantially.

questions.question: A woman reports dysuria and periurethral swelling. On examination, small ducts adjacent to the urethral opening are inflamed. Which structure is affected?
questions.explanation: Skene's ducts open within the urethra near the meatus and are prone to infection, often from organisms such as gonococci. Inflammation presents with dysuria and periurethral tenderness. This is distinct from Bartholin's glands, which lie more posteriorly in the labia majora.

questions.question: Values are described as guiding human behavior, decision-making, and actions. Which category of values specifically governs behavior in a particular profession?
questions.explanation: Professional values are the principles and standards that guide behavior in a specific profession or occupation. In nursing, professional values include principles such as beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, fidelity, and respect for patient autonomy. These values differ from personal or cultural values in that they are shaped by the norms, codes of ethics, and standards of a professional body or occupational group.

Autoerotic asphyxiation involves self-induced oxygen deprivation during sexual arousal to intensify orgasm, but it carries a serious risk of accidental death from loss of consciousness during the act. This distinguishes it from other paraphilias whose primary risks are infectious rather than fatal. Awareness of this risk is important for clinicians assessing unusual injury patterns.
questions.question: A man reports sexual arousal specifically tied to depriving himself of oxygen during masturbation, believing it intensifies orgasm. Which paraphilic practice is described, and what is its major danger?
options: Vampirism, which carries a risk of infection
Klismaphilia, which carries a risk of bowel injury
Urophilia, which carries a risk of urinary infection
Coprophilia, which carries a risk of gastrointestinal illness
Autoerotic asphyxiation, which carries a risk of accidental death

questions.explanation: UNFPA's role in safe motherhood is centred on funding, technical support, and commodities for reproductive and maternal health programmes, including family planning integration. This differs from UNICEF, whose mandate centres more broadly on child welfare. Recognising each agency's specific role helps coordinate multi-partner maternal health initiatives.
questions.question: A country partners with an international agency primarily known for funding reproductive health commodities and technical support for family planning and maternal health programmes. Which agency is most consistent with this role?

A nurse notices that a client's physiological response of increased heart rate, genital vasocongestion, and heightened sensation occurs during intimate contact. Which component of sexuality is being described?
questions.explanation: Sexual arousal involves physiological changes such as increased heart rate and genital vasocongestion in response to sexual stimuli, forming a key physical component of sexuality. This is distinct from psychological components such as body image or gender identity. Understanding this helps nurses address both physical and emotional dimensions of sexual health concerns.

questions.question: The Safe Motherhood Initiative focuses on which four leading causes of maternal death?
questions.explanation: The Safe Motherhood Initiative focuses on the four leading causes of maternal death: maternal sepsis, obstetric hemorrhage (severe bleeding), venous thromboembolism (blood clots), and severe hypertension in pregnancy (high blood pressure). These four conditions account for the majority of preventable maternal deaths globally and are the primary targets of evidence-based maternal health interventions within safe motherhood programs.
options: Maternal sepsis, obstetric hemorrhage, venous thromboembolism and severe hypertension
Anemia, obstructed labor, eclampsia and postpartum psychosis
Hemorrhage, malaria, HIV complications and urinary tract infections
Sepsis, trauma, malnutrition and cardiac complications in pregnancy
Hypertension, infection, obstructed labor and unsafe abortion

questions.question: A nurse observes that a community's shared expectations about modesty and family roles strongly shape how members interact with healthcare providers. Which category of values is being described?
questions.explanation: Social values are the shared beliefs and standards of behaviour recognised within a community or society, shaping expectations such as modesty and family roles. These often intersect with, but are distinct from, an individual's personal or professional values. Understanding social values helps nurses provide culturally attuned care.

An intimate relationship involves emotional closeness, vulnerability, and mutual trust between partners, extending beyond the purely physical dimension of sexuality. This differs from body image, which concerns self-perception, and sex role imagery, which concerns social role expectations. Recognising the emotional dimension broadens nursing assessment beyond physical sexual function alone.
questions.question: A nurse notes that a client's romantic partnership involves deep emotional closeness, vulnerability, and mutual trust beyond physical activity alone. Which sexuality-related concept is being described?

options: Female-factor infertility related to tubal patency
Combined infertility unrelated to either partner
Infertility caused solely by cervical factors
Male-factor infertility related to sperm production and quality
questions.explanation: Semen analysis is the primary diagnostic tool for evaluating male-factor infertility, assessing sperm count, motility, and morphology to identify production or quality defects. It has no direct role in assessing female ovulatory or tubal factors. A comprehensive infertility workup evaluates both partners in parallel.
questions.question: A man diagnosed with infertility undergoes semen analysis assessing sperm count, motility, and shape. For which broader category of male infertility is this test the primary diagnostic approach?

questions.explanation: One major objective of Family Life Education is to develop knowledge concerning the concept of family, its roles and functions. This helps individuals recognize the several tasks that need to be undertaken for the well-being and maintenance of the family. When individuals understand family roles and functions, they are better equipped to contribute to family stability and societal health.
options: Memorize government legislation related to family and marriage laws
Obtain employment in social welfare and community development agencies
Recognize tasks needed for the well-being and maintenance of the family unit
Gain academic qualifications in psychology or social sciences
Comply with traditional gender roles prescribed by religious authorities

Using only firm pressure throughout the examination
Using light, medium, and firm pressure levels
Using a single fixed pressure regardless of depth
Using pressure only around the nipple area
questions.question: During BSE palpation, a woman is taught to use varying pressure levels to feel tissue at different depths, including firm pressure for the tissue closest to the chest wall. What is this technique called?
questions.explanation: Effective BSE palpation involves using light pressure for tissue just under the skin, medium pressure for the middle tissue, and firm pressure to feel tissue closest to the chest wall and ribs. This graduated approach ensures thorough assessment of all breast tissue layers. Omitting firm pressure could miss deeper abnormalities.

Performed by female nurses when examining female clients
Conducted in a clinic setting without privacy screens
Documented in the patient's medical records for confidentiality reasons
Performed on clients above a specific age without specialist referral
questions.explanation: A common rule guiding reproductive organ examination is that when carrying out genital examinations, the nurse should be extra cautious of the patient's opinion about the examination and should not force it on the patient. Consent is paramount—patients have the right to refuse examination, and coercing or proceeding without consent violates patient autonomy and constitutes professional misconduct. Other rules include ensuring a chaperone is present, providing privacy, and refraining from offensive words or gestures.
